   6: developments are given in
   7: \cite{Kalman1963LinearSystems,TelekHorvath2007MinimalMAP,
   8: BladtNielsen2017MatrixExponential,MeszarosTelek2013DiscreteMAP2Canonical,
   9: PappTelek2013DiscretePHCanonical}.  We state the consequence needed to locate
  10: the visible fibre, classify the complete Markovian fibre of the physical
  11: two-state kernel, and then prove the higher-state quantitative assertion: at a
  12: minimal interior killed-reset kernel the admissible fibre has local dimension
  13: \((n-1)^2\).  Nonunique MAP and Coxian representatives are documented in
  14: \cite{RamirezCoboLilloWiper2010MAP2Nonidentifiability,
  15: RamirezCoboLillo2012WeakEquivalentMAP,RizkBurkeWalsh2019CoxianNonuniqueness}.
  16: Graph-specific time-to-event inverses are treated algebraically by
  17: Radulescu et al.\ \cite{RadulescuEtAl2025TimeToEventIdentifiability}; the
  18: criterion below instead isolates the exact orbit fibre for any declared
  19: minimal killed-reset subclass.
  20: 
  21: \paragraph{Recalled minimal-realization uniqueness.}
  22: Let \((a,A,b)\) and \((\widetilde a,\widetilde A,\widetilde b)\) be two real
  23: scalar realizations of the same dimension \(n\) such that
  24: \[
  25: aA^k b=\widetilde a\widetilde A^k\widetilde b
  26: \qquad(k\ge0).
  27: \]
  28: Assume that both reachability matrices
  29: \[
  30: [\,b,Ab,\ldots,A^{n-1}b\,],\qquad
  31: [\,\widetilde b,\widetilde A\widetilde b,\ldots,
  32: \widetilde A^{n-1}\widetilde b\,]
  33: \]
  34: and both observability matrices
  35: \[
  36: \begin{bmatrix}a\\aA\\\vdots\\aA^{n-1}\end{bmatrix},
  37: \qquad
  38: \begin{bmatrix}\widetilde a\\\widetilde a\widetilde A\\\vdots\\
  39: \widetilde a\widetilde A^{n-1}\end{bmatrix}
  40: \]
  41: have rank \(n\). Then there is a unique \(M\in\operatorname{GL}_n(\RR)\)
  42: such that
  43: \[
  44: \widetilde a=aM,
  45: \qquad \widetilde A=M^{-1}AM,
  46: \qquad \widetilde b=M^{-1}b.
  47: \]
  48: These rank hypotheses are precisely properties \textup{(R)} and \textup{(L)}
  49: of Bladt and Nielsen, whose Theorem~4.2.16 characterizes minimality by their
  50: simultaneous validity; the corresponding intertwining relations are given in
  51: their Lemmas~4.2.5--4.2.6
  52: \cite[Theorem~4.2.16, p.~216, and Lemmas~4.2.5--4.2.6,
  53: p.~212]{BladtNielsen2017MatrixExponential}. This standard result is invoked
  54: here and is not claimed as a new theorem; see also Kalman
  55: \cite{Kalman1963LinearSystems}, Telek--Horv\'ath
  56: \cite{TelekHorvath2007MinimalMAP}, and
  57: \cite{Ryden1996Aggregated,OCinneide1989PhaseTypeNonuniqueness,
  58: OCinneide1991InvariantPolytopes}.
  59: 
  60: \begin{proposition}[Recalled orbit-fibre consequence of minimal realization]
  61: \label{thm:nstate-killed-reset-identifiability-dichotomy-main}
  62: Fix \(n\ge2\), put \(\beta=e_n^\top\), and let
  63: \[
  64: \mathcal K_n=\{K\in\RR^{n\times n}:K\ge0,\ K\mathbf1\le\mathbf1,\
  65: \operatorname{spr}(K)<1\}.
  66: \]
  67: For \(K\in\mathcal K_n\), define the killed-reset D-MAP by
  68: \[
  69: T_0=K,\qquad T_1=(I-K)\mathbf1\beta
  70: \]
  71: and its Palm survival coordinates by \(S_k(K)=\beta K^k\mathbf1\).
  72: Call \(K\) minimal when both
  73: \[
  74: \mathcal C(K)=[\,\mathbf1,K\mathbf1,\ldots,K^{n-1}\mathbf1\,],
  75: \qquad
  76: \mathcal O(K)=
  77: \begin{bmatrix}\beta\\ \beta K\\ \vdots\\ \beta K^{n-1}\end{bmatrix}
  78: \]
  79: have rank \(n\). Let
  80: \[
  81: \mathcal G_n=\{M\in\operatorname{GL}_n(\RR):
  82: M\mathbf1=\mathbf1,\ \beta M=\beta\},
  83: \]
  84: and let \(\mathfrak P_n\subset\mathcal G_n\) be the reset-preserving
  85: permutation matrices.
  86: 
  87: For any declared subclass \(\mathcal C\subset\mathcal K_n\) of minimal
  88: kernels, fix the structural equivalence \(\sim_{\mathcal C}\) under which
  89: identification is requested, and assume that \(K\sim_{\mathcal C}L\) implies
  90: equality of visible laws. Examples are reset-preserving hidden-state
  91: relabeling and, in a serial rate chart, permutation of the rate coordinates.
  92: Define the Markovian orbit fibre
  93: \[
  94: \mathfrak F_{\mathcal C}(K)=
  95: \left\{M^{-1}KM\in\mathcal C:M\in\mathcal G_n\right\}
  96: \big/\!\sim_{\mathcal C}.
  97: \]
  98: Then standard minimal-realization uniqueness gives the following exact
  99: characterization.
 100: \begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
 101: \item Two minimal kernels \(K,L\in\mathcal K_n\) generate the same stationary
 102: visible click law if and only if
 103: \[
 104: \begin{aligned}
 105: L&=M^{-1}KM &&\text{for the unique }M\in\mathcal G_n\\
 106: &&&\text{implementing their normalized minimal realizations}.
 107: \end{aligned}
 108: \]
 109: \item Equivalently, the declared hidden object is identifiable from the visible law within
 110: \(\mathcal C\), modulo \(\sim_{\mathcal C}\), if and only if
 111: \[
 112: \#\mathfrak F_{\mathcal C}(K)=1\qquad\text{for every }K\in\mathcal C.
 113: \]
 114: Pointwise identifiability at \(K\) is equivalent to the same condition at
 115: that \(K\); if the cardinality exceeds one, its distinct classes are exactly
 116: the hidden nonidentifiability fibre. Thus this assertion is the orbit-fibre
 117: reformulation of part \textup{(i)}.
 118: \end{enumerate}
 119: Part~\textup{(ii)} is deliberately recorded only as terminology: after the
 120: fibre has been defined, singleton fibre and identifiability modulo
 121: \(\sim_{\mathcal C}\) are the same assertion.  Neither part is claimed as a
 122: new realization theorem.
 123: \end{proposition}
 124: 
 125: \begin{proof}
 126: The rank-one reset makes the visible process renewal; the displayed model
 127: specializes its restart law to a point mass. Its Palm gap tail is
 128: exactly \(S_k(K)\), so equality of visible stationary laws is equivalent to
 129: equality of all the scalar coordinates \(\beta K^k\mathbf1\), \(k\ge0\).
 130: Apply the minimal-realization theorem stated above to the triples
 131: \((\beta,K,\mathbf1)\) and \((\beta,L,\mathbf1)\). Its hypotheses are exactly
 132: the two displayed rank conditions in the proposition, and it gives a unique
 133: similarity \(L=M^{-1}KM\). Preservation of the fixed input and output vectors
 134: gives \(M\mathbf1=\mathbf1\) and \(\beta M=\beta\), respectively.
 135: Conversely, these two identities give
 136: \[
 137: \beta(M^{-1}KM)^k\mathbf1=\beta K^k\mathbf1
 138: \]
 139: for every \(k\), proving (i). Taking the intersection with
 140: \(\mathcal C\) and then quotienting precisely the declared structural
 141: equivalence proves
 142: the necessary-and-sufficient assertion (ii).
 143: \end{proof}
 144: 
 145: \begin{theorem}[Complete two-state fibre arc and exchange dichotomy]
 146: \label{thm:two-state-complete-fibre-arc-main}
 147: Under \Cref{ass:model-inference-contract-main}, put \(K=T_0\),
 148: \(q_\ast=\Gamma/\kappa_{\mathrm r}\), and
 149: \[
 150:  I_\ast=[\min\{1,q_\ast\},\max\{1,q_\ast\}].
 151: \]
 152: Then \(K\) is minimal, and its complete visible-law fibre in
 153: \(\mathcal K_2\) is the injectively parametrized closed arc
 154: \[
 155:  \{K(q):q\in I_\ast\},
 156:  \qquad
 157:  K(q)=
 158:  \begin{pmatrix}
 159:  p-b+bq & \displaystyle\frac{b(1-q)(q-q_\ast)}q\\[5pt]
 160:  bq & s+b(1-q)
 161:  \end{pmatrix}.
 162:  \tag{F1}
 163: \]
 164: Here complete means that every \(L\in\mathcal K_2\) with the same stationary
 165: visible click law as \(K\) is \(K(q)\) for exactly one \(q\in I_\ast\).
 166: Writing \(T_0(\alpha,\eta)\) for the no-click kernel constructed with attempt
 167: rate \(\alpha\) and recovery rate \(\eta\), the endpoints are the two physical
 168: triangular kernels obtained by exchanging those rates:
 169: \[
 170:  K(1)=T_0(\Gamma,\kappa_{\mathrm r}),
 171:  \qquad
 172:  K(q_\ast)=T_0(\kappa_{\mathrm r},\Gamma).
 173:  \tag{F2}
 174: \]
 175: If \(\Gamma\ne\kappa_{\mathrm r}\), every \(q\) strictly between the
 176: endpoints gives a strictly positive kernel with strictly positive killing
 177: deficits, and the physical triangular subfamily meets the arc only at the two
 178: endpoints.  If \(\Gamma=\kappa_{\mathrm r}\), then \(I_\ast=\{1\}\), so
 179: the entire two-state killed-reset fibre is a singleton.  Thus the unrestricted
 180: two-state hidden kernel is identifiable exactly on the exchange diagonal and
 181: has a continuum fibre off it; within the physical sampled-counter subfamily,
 182: the only ambiguity off the diagonal is the rate exchange.
 183: \end{theorem}
 184: 
 185: \begin{proof}
 186: First \(b>0\).  If \(\Gamma\ne\kappa_{\mathrm r}\), direct evaluation of
 187: the defining integral gives
 188: \[
 189:  b=\frac{\kappa_{\mathrm r}(p-s)}{\kappa_{\mathrm r}-\Gamma},
 190:  \qquad
 191:  b+s-p=\frac{\Gamma(p-s)}{\kappa_{\mathrm r}-\Gamma}
 192:           =bq_\ast>0.
 193:  \tag{F3}
 194: \]
 195: The same identities hold by continuity on the diagonal, where
 196: \(p=s\), \(b=\Gamma\Delta\tau p>0\), and \(q_\ast=1\).  Consequently
 197: \[
 198:  \det[\mathbf1,K\mathbf1]=b+s-p=bq_\ast>0,
 199:  \qquad
 200:  \det\begin{bmatrix}e_2^\top\\e_2^\top K\end{bmatrix}=-b\ne0,
 201: \]
 202: so \(K\) is minimal.
 203: 
 204: Every member of \(\mathcal G_2\) has the unique form
 205: \[
 206:  M_q=\begin{pmatrix}q&1-q\\0&1\end{pmatrix},\qquad q\ne0.
 207: \]
 208: Multiplication, using \(b+s-p=bq_\ast\), gives
 209: \(M_q^{-1}KM_q=K(q)\) in \textup{(F1)}.  Since \(K\) is minimal, its scalar
 210: Hankel sequence has rank two.  Any \(L\in\mathcal K_2\) with the same visible
 211: law has the same leading Hankel matrix; its factorization as
 212: \(\mathcal O(L)\mathcal C(L)\) has rank two, so both factors have rank two and
 213: \(L\) is minimal as well.  The recalled orbit--fibre proposition therefore
 214: forces every such \(L\) to have the displayed form.  If
 215: \(K(q)\in\mathcal K_2\), its lower-left entry
 216: is \(bq\ge0\).  Invertibility excludes \(q=0\), hence \(q>0\).  Its
 217: upper-right entry then yields the exact condition
 218: \[
 219:  \frac{b(1-q)(q-q_\ast)}q\ge0
 220:  \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad q\in I_\ast.
 221:  \tag{F4}
 222: \]
 223: 
 224: Conversely, let \(q\in I_\ast\).  The two diagonal entries in
 225: \textup{(F1)} are affine in \(q\), with endpoint values \(p,s\) and \(s,p\),
 226: respectively, and are therefore positive.  The lower-left entry is positive,
 227: and \textup{(F4)} makes the upper-right entry nonnegative.  Writing
 228: \(a=1-b-s>0\), the two killing deficits are
 229: \[
 230:  \mathbf1-K(q)\mathbf1
 231:  =\begin{pmatrix}a+bq_\ast/q\\a\end{pmatrix}>0.
 232:  \tag{F5}
 233: \]
 234: Similarity preserves the spectral radius
 235: \(\max\{p,s\}<1\), so \(K(q)\in\mathcal K_2\).  This proves that the
 236: displayed arc is the complete fibre.  It is injective because its lower-left
 237: entry is \(bq\).
 238: 
 239: At \(q=1\) one recovers \(K\).  At \(q=q_\ast\),
 240: \[
 241:  K(q_\ast)=\begin{pmatrix}s&0\\bq_\ast&p\end{pmatrix}.
 242: \]
 243: Equation~\textup{(F3)} says that \(bq_\ast\) is precisely the no-click
 244: recovery-to-ready probability after exchanging the two rates, and its second
 245: row has the same killing deficit \(a\); this proves \textup{(F2)}.  If
 246: \(q_\ast\ne1\), the product in the upper-right entry is strictly positive
 247: inside \(I_\ast\) and vanishes only at its endpoints.  All remaining entries
 248: and both deficits are already strict there.  If \(q_\ast=1\),
 249: \textup{(F4)} forces \(q=1\).  The endpoint, triangular-intersection, and
 250: identifiability statements follow.
 251: \end{proof}
 252: 
 253: The generalized-Erlang representation and its Coxian minimality theory are due
 254: to He--Zhang \cite{HeZhang2009GeneralizedErlang,HeZhang2008MinimalCoxian}.
 255: The following corollary is their serial phase-type structure specialized to
 256: finitely many sampled Palm-tail coordinates; the confluent calculation records
 257: how repeated rates remain recoverable in that specialization.
 258: 
 259: \begin{corollary}[Finite-coordinate serial specialization with collisions]
 260: \label{cor:nstate-serial-all-collision-identifiability-main}
 261: Fix \(n\ge2\), a known \(\Delta\tau>0\), and arbitrary positive rates
 262: \(\theta=(\theta_1,\ldots,\theta_n)\), with repetitions allowed. Let
 263: \[
 264: Q(\theta)_{ii}=-\theta_i,\qquad
 265: Q(\theta)_{i,i-1}=\theta_i\quad(2\le i\le n),
 266: \]
 267: with all other entries zero, and put
 268: \[
 269: T_0(\theta)=e^{\Delta\tau Q(\theta)},\qquad
 270: T_1(\theta)=(I-T_0(\theta))\mathbf1e_n^\top.
 271: \]
 272: Then the visible record identifies exactly the unordered rate multiset
 273: \(\{\!\{\theta_1,\ldots,\theta_n\}\!\}\). Equivalently, the fibre of the
 274: labelled serial parameter is its \(\mathfrak S_n\)-permutation orbit.
 275: 
 276: More explicitly, if the distinct rates are
 277: \(\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_r\) with multiplicities
 278: \(m_1,\ldots,m_r\), and \(z_j=e^{-\lambda_j\Delta\tau}\), then the Palm tail
 279: has the confluent Prony form
 280: \[
 281: S_k=\sum_{j=1}^r\sum_{\ell=0}^{m_j-1}
 282: c_{j\ell}k^\ell z_j^k,\qquad c_{j,m_j-1}\ne0,
 283: \]
 284: and its minimal recurrence polynomial is
 285: \[
 286: \chi_\theta(x)=\prod_{j=1}^r(x-z_j)^{m_j}.
 287: \]
 288: The leading \(n\times n\) Hankel matrix
 289: \((S_{i+j})_{0\le i,j<n}\) is invertible; hence
 290: \(S_0,\ldots,S_{2n-1}\) determine \(\chi_\theta\), including all collision
 291: multiplicities. Pole collision therefore changes conditioning and the local
 292: root chart, but does not change population identifiability.
 293: \end{corollary}
 294: 
 295: \begin{proof}
 296: Starting in phase \(n\), the absorption time is
 297: \(W=X_n+\cdots+X_1\), where the \(X_i\) are independent exponentials with
 298: rates \(\theta_i\). Its Laplace transform is
 299: \[
 300: \EE e^{-sW}=\prod_{i=1}^n\frac{\theta_i}{s+\theta_i}.
 301: \]
 302: Consequently
 303: \[
 304: \int_0^\infty e^{-st}\PP(W>t)\,dt
 305: =\frac{1-\prod_{i=1}^n\theta_i/(s+\theta_i)}{s}
 306: \]
 307: has at
 308: \(-\lambda_j\) a pole of exact order \(m_j\). Partial-fraction inversion and
 309: sampling at \(t=k\Delta\tau\) give the displayed exponential-polynomial form
 310: with nonzero top confluent coefficient. Standard confluent Prony algebra
 311: then gives the exact minimal annihilator \(\chi_\theta\)
 312: \cite{KunisRoemerVonDerOhe2020Prony}.
 313: 
 314: For completeness of the finite-coordinate assertion, the matrices
 315: \(\mathcal O(Q)\) and \(\mathcal C(Q)\) are nonsingular: successive rows
 316: \(e_n^\top Q^j\) and successive columns \(Q^j\mathbf1\) expose the nonzero
 317: bidiagonal products triangularly. Because the exponential is injective on
 318: the real spectrum of \(Q\), Hermite interpolation supplies a polynomial
 319: \(p\) with \(Q=p(e^{\Delta\tau Q})\); hence the corresponding observation and
 320: reachability spaces for \(T_0=e^{\Delta\tau Q}\) are also full. Therefore
 321: \[
 322: (S_{i+j})_{0\le i,j<n}=\mathcal O(T_0)\mathcal C(T_0)
 323: \]
 324: is invertible, and the first \(2n\) tails solve uniquely for the order-\(n\)
 325: recurrence. The roots and their algebraic multiplicities recover
 326: \(\lambda_j=-\Delta\tau^{-1}\log z_j\) and \(m_j\). Conversely, permuting
 327: the independent summands does not change \(W\), the Palm gap law, or the
 328: stationary renewal law. This proves the exact fibre claim.
 329: \end{proof}
 330: 
 331: \begin{theorem}[Quantitative interior fibre dimension and positivity persistence]
 332: \label{thm:nstate-interior-continuum-nonidentifiability-main}
 333: For the unrestricted class with \(\sim_{\mathcal K_n}\) equal to
 334: reset-preserving state relabelling, the hidden kernel is locally
 335: nonidentifiable at every minimal interior point \(K\), where interior means
 336: \(K>0\) and \((I-K)\mathbf1>0\) entrywise. More precisely, the
 337: reset-preserving similarity group has Lie algebra
 338: \[
 339: \mathfrak g_n=\{B:B\mathbf1=0,\ \beta B=0\},
 340: \qquad \dim\mathfrak g_n=(n-1)^2,
 341: \]
 342: and the orbit map
 343: \[
 344: \psi_K:\mathcal G_n\longrightarrow\mathbb R^{n\times n},\qquad
 345: \psi_K(M)=M^{-1}KM,
 346: \]
 347: has injective differential
 348: \[
 349: D\psi_K(I)B=[K,B]\qquad(B\in\mathfrak g_n).
 350: \]
 351: Consequently the visible fibre through \(K\) contains, in a neighbourhood of
 352: \(K\), a smooth immersed manifold of dimension exactly \((n-1)^2\).  Every
 353: kernel on a sufficiently small neighbourhood of this orbit manifold remains
 354: strictly substochastic: its entries and killing deficits are positive.  After
 355: quotienting by the finite reset-preserving permutation group, the local fibre
 356: still has dimension \((n-1)^2\).
 357: \end{theorem}
 358: 
 359: \begin{proof}
 360: Because \(\beta\mathbf1=1\),
 361: \(\RR^n=\operatorname{span}\{\mathbf1\}\oplus\ker\beta\).  Relative to this
 362: decomposition, \(B\mathbf1=0\) removes the first block column and
 363: \(\beta B=0\) forces the range into \(\ker\beta\).  Thus
 364: \(B=\operatorname{diag}(0,A)\), with arbitrary
 365: \(A\in\operatorname{End}(\ker\beta)\), and
 366: \(\dim\mathfrak g_n=(n-1)^2\).
 367: 
 368: Differentiating \(\exp(-tB)K\exp(tB)\) at zero gives
 369: \(D\psi_K(I)B=[K,B]\).  Suppose \([K,B]=0\).  Since \(B\mathbf1=0\),
 370: \[
 371: BK^j\mathbf1=K^jB\mathbf1=0,
 372: \qquad j=0,\ldots,n-1.
 373: \]
 374: The reachability matrix
 375: \([\mathbf1,K\mathbf1,\ldots,K^{n-1}\mathbf1]\) has rank \(n\), so these
 376: equalities imply \(B=0\).  Hence the differential is injective on all of
 377: \(\mathfrak g_n\), not merely in one selected direction.
 378: 
 379: The constant-rank theorem now makes the image of \(\psi_K\) near the identity
 380: a smooth immersed manifold of dimension \((n-1)^2\).  For every
 381: \(M\in\mathcal G_n\),
 382: \[
 383: \beta\psi_K(M)^j\mathbf1=\beta K^j\mathbf1\qquad(j\ge0),
 384: \]
 385: so the recalled orbit-fibre result places this entire manifold in the visible
 386: fibre.  Finally, all entries of \(M^{-1}KM\) and all components of
 387: \((I-M^{-1}KM)\mathbf1\) depend continuously on \(M\).  Their values at
 388: \(M=I\) are strictly positive; a sufficiently small identity neighbourhood
 389: therefore remains inside the interior Markovian cone.  The stabilizer has zero
 390: Lie algebra by injectivity of the differential, and quotienting by the finite
 391: reset-preserving permutation group cannot change local dimension.  This proves
 392: all assertions.
 393: \end{proof}
 394: 
 395: \begin{remark}[Nonminimal and graph-specific open interfaces]
 396: \label{rem:nstate-identifiability-open-interfaces-main}
 397: The characterization and the two headline results deliberately assume
 398: Hankel/minimal rank \(n\). If a nominal
 399: \(n\)-state representation has lower visible rank, equal laws need not be
 400: related by an invertible \(n\times n\) similarity; a sharp classification then
 401: requires a stratified treatment of nonminimal augmentations. For a fixed
 402: nonserial zero pattern on the boundary of the Markovian cone, evaluating the
 403: orbit intersection \(\mathfrak F_{\mathcal C}(K)\) is an exact semialgebraic
 404: problem, but no graph-uniform closed form is claimed here. Finally, collision
 405: multiplicity is population-identifiable in the serial model but statistically
 406: singular under noisy finite records. These are explicit interfaces, not
 407: consequences of the present results.
 408: \end{remark}
 409: 
 410: For orientation, the unrestricted fibre is already nontrivial in two states:
 411: \[
 412: K=\begin{pmatrix}1/2&0\\1/2&1/4\end{pmatrix},\qquad
 413: M=\begin{pmatrix}9/10&1/10\\0&1\end{pmatrix},\qquad
 414: M^{-1}KM=\begin{pmatrix}9/20&1/45\\9/20&3/10\end{pmatrix}.
 415: \]
 416: Both kernels are nonnegative and substochastic,
 417: \(M\mathbf1=\mathbf1\), \(e_2^\top M=e_2^\top\), and their entire visible
 418: renewal laws coincide, although the hidden kernels do not.

   1: \section{Stationary collision experiments for sampled serial phase-type renewals}
   2: \label{sec:stationary-serial-collision-main}
   3: 
   4: This section changes the inferential object from a deterministic product of
   5: complete Palm gaps to the stationary binary record itself.  We first close
   6: that gap for the present two-state sampled counter and then treat one isolated
   7: double collision in an arbitrary fixed serial order.  Throughout this section
   8: the sampling interval \(\Delta\tau>0\) is known.  The record is the lattice
   9: renewal indicator obtained by binning the serial absorption time under the
  10: reset-and-boundary construction; it is not a generic discretely sampled event
  11: process, and multiple post-click renewals within a bin are excluded by that
  12: construction.
  13: 
  14: For two finite multisets \(A=\{\!\{a_1,\ldots,a_n\}\!\}\) and
  15: \(B=\{\!\{b_1,\ldots,b_n\}\!\}\), write
  16: \[
  17:  d_{\rm m}(A,B)=\min_{\pi\in\mathfrak S_n}
  18:        \max_{1\le i\le n}|a_i-b_{\pi(i)}|
  19: \tag{SC1}
  20: \]
  21: for optimal-matching distance.  This metric retains multiplicities.

  23: \begin{paperthm}[Stationary two-state exchange experiment and sharp recovery]
  24: \label{thm:stationary-two-state-collision-main}
  25: Fix \(0<\varepsilon<M<\infty\).  In the sampled-counter model of
  26: \Cref{ass:model-inference-contract-main}, use the quotient coordinates
  27: \[
  28:  c=\frac{\Gamma+\kappa_{\mathrm r}}2,
  29:  \qquad d=\frac{\Gamma-\kappa_{\mathrm r}}2,
  30:  \qquad \delta=d^2\ge0.
  31: \tag{SC2}
  32: \]
  33: Let \(P_{c,\delta}^{(N)}\) be the law of the stationary binary record
  34: \((A_0,\ldots,A_{N-1})\), and let \(g_{c,\delta}\), \(S_{c,\delta}\), and
  35: \(\mu_{c,\delta}=\sum_{k\ge0}S_{c,\delta}(k)\) denote its Palm gap mass,
  36: tail, and mean cycle length.  At \(\delta=0\), set
  37: \[
  38:  \dot\ell_c(k)=\partial_c\log g_{c,0}(k),\qquad
  39:  \dot\ell_\delta(k)=\partial_\delta\log g_{c,\delta}(k)|_{\delta=0},
  40: \]
  41: and define the calendar information
  42: \[
  43:  I_2(c)=\frac1{\mu_{c,0}}
  44:  \sum_{k\ge0}g_{c,0}(k)
  45:  \begin{pmatrix}\dot\ell_c(k)\\ \dot\ell_\delta(k)\end{pmatrix}
  46:  \begin{pmatrix}\dot\ell_c(k)&\dot\ell_\delta(k)\end{pmatrix}.
  47: \tag{SC3}
  48: \]
  49: Then the following conclusions hold uniformly for \(c\in[\varepsilon,M]\).
  50: 
  51: \begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)},leftmargin=2.6em]
  52: \item If \(u\in\RR\) and \(v\in[0,\infty)\) range over bounded sets, then
  53: \[
  54:  \log\frac{dP_{c+u/\sqrt N,v/\sqrt N}^{(N)}}
  55:                {dP_{c,0}^{(N)}}
  56:  =\begin{pmatrix}u\\v\end{pmatrix}^{\!\top}\Delta_{N,c}
  57:  -\frac12\begin{pmatrix}u\\v\end{pmatrix}^{\!\top}
  58:  I_2(c)\begin{pmatrix}u\\v\end{pmatrix}+o_{P_{c,0}}(1),
  59: \tag{SC4}
  60: \]
  61: where the remainder is uniform in \((c,u,v)\) and
  62: \(\Delta_{N,c}\Rightarrow\mathcal N_2\{0,I_2(c)\}\) uniformly in bounded
  63: Lipschitz distance.  Thus the stationary-record experiments converge to the
  64: Gaussian shift on the half-plane \(\RR\times[0,\infty)\).
  65: 
  66: \item The continuous survival transform has a double pole at the collision,
  67: whereas its collision derivative has an exact fourth-order pole:
  68: \[
  69:  \mathcal L\{\overline F_{c,\delta}\}(s)
  70:  =\frac1s\left\{1-
  71:  \frac{c^2-\delta}{(s+c)^2-\delta}\right\},
  72: \quad
  73:  \partial_\delta\mathcal L\{\overline F_{c,\delta}\}(s)|_0
  74:  =\frac{s+2c}{(s+c)^4}.
  75: \tag{SC5}
  76: \]
  77: The centre derivative is \(-2c/(s+c)^3\).  Consequently the sampled
  78: collision derivative contains a nonzero
  79: \(k^3e^{-c\Delta\tau k}\) term, while the centre derivative has degree at
  80: most two at that exponential base.  Hence
  81: \[
  82:  \inf_{c\in[\varepsilon,M]}\lambda_{\min}\{I_2(c)\}>0.
  83: \tag{SC6}
  84: \]
  85: 
  86: \item Partition \(I_2\) according to \((c,\delta)\) and put
  87: \[
  88:  J_2(c)=I_{\delta\delta}
  89:  -I_{\delta c}I_{cc}^{-1}I_{c\delta}>0.
  90: \tag{SC7}
  91: \]
  92: For testing \(H_0:\delta=0\) against \(H_1:\delta>0\), the residualized
  93: score test is asymptotically level \(\alpha\) uniformly in \(c\).  It
  94: coincides with the likelihood-ratio rule only in the limiting Gaussian
  95: half-plane experiment.  At
  96: \((c_N,\delta_N)=(c+u/\sqrt N,v/\sqrt N)\) its limiting power is
  97: \[
  98:  1-\Phi_{\rm N}\{z_{1-\alpha}-v\sqrt{J_2(c)}\}.
  99: \tag{SC8}
 100: \]
 101: This is the Gaussian half-plane power envelope among tests with uniform local
 102: asymptotic level \(\alpha\).
 103: 
 104: \item There is an estimator \(\widehat{\mathcal R}_N\) of the unordered rate
 105: pair such that, uniformly for bounded \((u,v)\),
 106: \[
 107:  d_{\rm m}\left(
 108:  \widehat{\mathcal R}_N,
 109:  \{\!\{c+u/\sqrt N+\sqrt{v/\sqrt N},
 110:           c+u/\sqrt N-\sqrt{v/\sqrt N}\}\!\}\right)
 111:  =O_P(N^{-1/4}).
 112: \tag{SC9}
 113: \]
 114: The estimated centre is root-\(N\), and the estimator first obtains a
 115: root-\(N\) estimate of \(\delta\) and projects it onto \([0,\infty)\).
 116: Conversely, for every fixed \(c\in(\varepsilon,M)\), \(v_0>0\), and
 117: \(0<a<\sqrt{v_0}/2\),
 118: \[
 119:  \liminf_{N\to\infty}\ \inf_{\widehat{\mathcal R}_N}
 120:  \max_{v\in\{0,v_0\}}
 121:  P_{c,v/\sqrt N}^{(N)}\!\left\{
 122:  N^{1/4}d_{\rm m}(\widehat{\mathcal R}_N,
 123:  \{\!\{c+\sqrt{v/\sqrt N},c-\sqrt{v/\sqrt N}\}\!\})>a
 124:  \right\}>0.
 125: \tag{SC10}
 126: \]
 127: Thus \(N^{-1/4}\) is uniformly attainable and pointwise locally
 128: minimax-optimal in rate, as witnessed by this fixed-base two-point threshold
 129: lower bound.  No exact minimax-risk constant is asserted.  The sign of \(d\)
 130: is not identifiable.
 131: \end{enumerate}
 132: \end{paperthm}
 133: 
 134: We now impose exactly the isolated-collision restrictions used in the
 135: higher-order result.  Fix \(n\ge2\), \(0<\varepsilon<M<\infty\), and
 136: \(c_0>0\).  The compact double-rate stratum is
 137: \[
 138: \mathcal C_{n}(\varepsilon,M,c_0)=
 139: \left\{(\lambda,\lambda,\lambda_3,\ldots,\lambda_n):
 140: \begin{array}{l}
 141: \lambda,\lambda_j\in[\varepsilon,M],\\
 142: \lambda_3<\cdots<\lambda_n,\\
 143: |\lambda_j-\lambda|\ge c_0,\\
 144: |\lambda_i-\lambda_j|\ge c_0\quad(3\le i<j\le n)
 145: \end{array}\right\}.
 146: \tag{SC11}
 147: \]
 148: Only one double collision is allowed; all other rates are simple and uniformly
 149: separated.  The inequalities in \textup{(SC11)} canonically order the
 150: noncollision rates (and are vacuous for \(n=2\)); these coordinates are not
 151: labels of physical serial states.  No assertion below covers simultaneous
 152: collisions, unknown order, unknown sampling interval, or nonserial phase-type
 153: representations.
 154: 
 155: \begin{paperthm}[Stationary double-pole experiment for sampled generalized-Erlang renewals]
 156: \label{thm:stationary-serial-double-pole-main}
 157: Fix \(n\), \(\varepsilon,M,c_0\), and known \(\Delta\tau>0\) as above, and
 158: suppose \(\mathcal C_n(\varepsilon,M,c_0)\ne\varnothing\).  For
 159: \(\theta=(\theta_1,\ldots,\theta_n)\), let
 160: \[
 161:  Q(\theta)_{ii}=-\theta_i,\qquad
 162:  Q(\theta)_{i,i-1}=\theta_i\quad(2\le i\le n),
 163: \quad K_\theta=e^{\Delta\tau Q(\theta)},
 164: \quad T_{1,\theta}=(I-K_\theta)\mathbf1e_n^\top.
 165: \tag{SC12}
 166: \]
 167: Let \(P_\theta^{(N)}\) be the stationary length-\(N\) binary record from the
 168: killed-reset kernels \((K_\theta,T_{1,\theta})\).  Near the displayed
 169: stratum use
 170: \[
 171:  c=\frac{\theta_1+\theta_2}{2},\qquad
 172: \delta=\left(\frac{\theta_1-\theta_2}{2}\right)^2\ge0,
 173: \qquad \eta=(c,\theta_3,\ldots,\theta_n)\in\RR^{n-1}.
 174: \tag{SC13}
 175: \]
 176: Here and below the separated entries of \(\eta\) are in the canonical order
 177: of \textup{(SC11)}.  Bounded root-\(N\) perturbations preserve this order for
 178: all sufficiently large \(N\), uniformly on the stratum.
 179: Write \(g_{\eta,\delta}\), \(S_{\eta,\delta}\), and
 180: \(\mu_{\eta,\delta}\) for the Palm gap mass, tail, and mean cycle length,
 181: and at \((\eta_0,0)\) put
 182: \[
 183:  \dot\ell_{\eta,\delta}(k)
 184:  =\nabla_{(\eta,\delta)}\log g_{\eta,\delta}(k)|_{(\eta_0,0)},
 185:  \qquad
 186:  I_n(\eta_0)=\frac1{\mu_{\eta_0,0}}
 187:  \sum_{k\ge0}g_{\eta_0,0}(k)
 188:  \dot\ell_{\eta,\delta}(k)\dot\ell_{\eta,\delta}(k)^\top.
 189: \tag{SC14}
 190: \]
 191: Then:
 192: 
 193: \begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)},leftmargin=2.6em]
 194: \item For bounded \(u\in\RR^{n-1}\) and \(v\in[0,\infty)\), uniformly over
 195: \((\eta_0,0)\in\mathcal C_n(\varepsilon,M,c_0)\),
 196: \[
 197:  \log\frac{dP_{\eta_0+u/\sqrt N,v/\sqrt N}^{(N)}}
 198:                {dP_{\eta_0,0}^{(N)}}
 199:  =\begin{pmatrix}u\\v\end{pmatrix}^{\!\top}\Delta_{N,\eta_0}
 200:  -\frac12\begin{pmatrix}u\\v\end{pmatrix}^{\!\top}
 201:  I_n(\eta_0)\begin{pmatrix}u\\v\end{pmatrix}
 202:  +o_{P_{\eta_0,0}}(1),
 203: \tag{SC15}
 204: \]
 205: and \(\Delta_{N,\eta_0}\Rightarrow
 206: \mathcal N_n\{0,I_n(\eta_0)\}\) uniformly in bounded Lipschitz distance.
 207: The local stationary-record experiments therefore converge to the Gaussian
 208: shift on \(\RR^{n-1}\times[0,\infty)\).
 209: 
 210: \item The information is uniformly nondegenerate:
 211: \[
 212:  \inf_{\eta_0\in\mathcal C_n(\varepsilon,M,c_0)}
 213:  \lambda_{\min}\{I_n(\eta_0)\}>0.
 214: \tag{SC16}
 215: \]
 216: This follows from sampled pole order, not merely from population
 217: identifiability: the \(\delta\)-derivative has a nonzero
 218: \(k^3e^{-\lambda\Delta\tau k}\) component; the centre derivative reaches
 219: degree two at that base; and the derivative of each separated rate has a
 220: unique degree-one component at its own exponential base.
 221: 
 222: \item Partition \(I_n\) according to \((\eta,\delta)\), and set
 223: \[
 224:  J_n=I_{\delta\delta}
 225:  -I_{\delta\eta}I_{\eta\eta}^{-1}I_{\eta\delta}>0.
 226: \tag{SC17}
 227: \]
 228: Choose before observing the record a compact null-coordinate neighbourhood
 229: \(\mathcal E_0\) whose interior contains the \(\eta\)-projection of the
 230: compact stratum and whose closure lies in the common score chart supplied by
 231: \Cref{lem:uniform-sampled-bin-tail-score-main}.  For \(\eta\in\mathcal E_0\),
 232: write
 233: \[
 234:  s_{\eta,0}(k)
 235:  =\left.\nabla_{(\eta,\delta)}\log g_{\eta,\delta}(k)
 236:    \right|_{\delta=0}
 237:  =\begin{pmatrix}s_{\rm nuis}(k;\eta)\\s_\delta(k;\eta)\end{pmatrix},
 238:  \qquad
 239:  I_N(\eta)=\frac1N\sum_{j=1}^{K_N}
 240:  s_{\eta,0}(G_j)s_{\eta,0}(G_j)^\top,
 241: \]
 242: and partition \(I_N\) in the same order; set \(I_N(\eta)=0\) outside
 243: \(\mathcal E_0\).  Define its empirical Schur complement totally by
 244: \[
 245:  J_N(\eta)=
 246:  \begin{cases}
 247:  I_{\delta\delta,N}(\eta)
 248:  -I_{\delta\eta,N}(\eta)I_{\eta\eta,N}(\eta)^{-1}
 249:   I_{\eta\delta,N}(\eta),
 250:  &\eta\in\mathcal E_0\ \text{and}\
 251:   \lambda_{\min}\{I_{\eta\eta,N}(\eta)\}>0,\\
 252:  0,&\text{otherwise}.
 253:  \end{cases}
 254: \]
 255: For the measurable recurrence fit \(\widehat\eta_N\) in
 256: \Cref{lem:serial-collision-recurrence-estimator-main}, let
 257: \[
 258:  \mathcal G_N=\{\widehat\eta_N\in\mathcal E_0,
 259:                  J_N(\widehat\eta_N)>0\}.
 260: \]
 261: On \(\mathcal G_N\), set
 262: \[
 263:  Z_N=\frac{N^{-1/2}\sum_{j=1}^{K_N}
 264:  \left[s_\delta(G_j;\widehat\eta_N)
 265:  -I_{\delta\eta,N}(\widehat\eta_N)
 266:   I_{\eta\eta,N}(\widehat\eta_N)^{-1}
 267:   s_{\rm nuis}(G_j;\widehat\eta_N)\right]}
 268:  {\sqrt{J_N(\widehat\eta_N)}}
 269: \]
 270: and let \(\phi_N=\mathbf1_{\{Z_N>z_{1-\alpha}\}}\); off
 271: \(\mathcal G_N\), define \(\phi_N=0\).  Thus the fit being outside the score
 272: chart, a singular empirical nuisance block, and a nonpositive empirical Schur
 273: complement all give no rejection.  These piecewise definitions and the Borel
 274: recurrence fit make \(\phi_N\) a total measurable function of every binary
 275: record.  This gate is asymptotically inactive uniformly on the stated local
 276: families.  The residualized score test is uniformly asymptotically level
 277: \(\alpha\) and attains the Gaussian half-space
 278: power envelope.  Specifically, \(\phi_N\) has uniform asymptotic level
 279: \(\alpha\) for \(H_0:\delta=0\) and, at \(\delta_N=v/\sqrt N\), has
 280: nuisance-adjusted limiting power
 281: \[
 282:  1-\Phi_{\rm N}\{z_{1-\alpha}-v\sqrt{J_n(\eta_0)}\}.
 283: \tag{SC18}
 284: \]
 285: 
 286: \item A measurable finite-atlas recurrence estimator based on the first
 287: \(2n\) empirical complete-gap tails gives root-\(N\) estimates of the
 288: canonically ordered \((\eta,\delta)\), after projection of \(\delta\) onto
 289: \([0,\infty)\).  The induced unordered-multiset estimator
 290: \(\widehat{\mathcal R}_{n,N}\) satisfies, uniformly over the compact stratum
 291: and bounded \((u,v)\),
 292: \[
 293:  d_{\rm m}(\widehat{\mathcal R}_{n,N},
 294:  \{\!\{c_N+\sqrt{\delta_N},c_N-\sqrt{\delta_N},
 295:           \theta_{3,N},\ldots,\theta_{n,N}\}\!\})=O_P(N^{-1/4}),
 296: \tag{SC19}
 297: \]
 298: where \((\eta_N,\delta_N)=(\eta_0+u/\sqrt N,v/\sqrt N)\).  The centre and
 299: all canonically ordered separated rates are root-\(N\).
 300: 
 301: For every fixed point of the stratum, every \(v_0>0\), and every
 302: \(0<a<\sqrt{v_0}/2\), the analogue of \textup{(SC10)}, with the remaining
 303: rates held fixed, has a strictly positive lower limit, bounded below by the
 304: Gaussian two-point testing constant displayed in
 305: \Cref{lem:two-point-threshold-rate-main}.  Hence the unordered-multiset rate
 306: \(N^{-1/4}\) is uniformly attainable over compact bounded local alternatives
 307: and is pointwise locally minimax-optimal in rate at every collision base, as
 308: witnessed by a two-point threshold-risk lower bound.  This is a rate statement,
 309: not an exact asymptotic minimax-risk or sharp-constant theorem.
 310: \end{enumerate}
 311: \end{paperthm}
 312: 
 313: \noindent\textbf{Limiting-experiment likelihood-ratio remark.}
 314: In the limiting Gaussian half-space experiment, maximizing the quadratic
 315: Gaussian likelihood over \(v\ge0\) gives the same rejection rule as the
 316: residualized score test.  Thus the residualized score test coincides with the
 317: likelihood-ratio test in the limiting Gaussian experiment.  No finite-record
 318: local likelihood-ratio statistic or argmax transfer is asserted.

   1: \subsection{Stationary likelihood reduction and the two-state proof}
   2: \label{subsec:stationary-renewal-lan-proof-main}
   3: 
   4: We use the following renewal lemma with a finite-dimensional parameter
   5: \(q\).  Its uniform formulation is included because replacing a deterministic
   6: number of Palm gaps by the stationary record is essential here.
   7: 
   8: \begin{lemma}[Compact-uniform stationary renewal LAN]
   9: \label{lem:compact-uniform-stationary-renewal-lan-main}
  10: Let \(\mathcal Q_0\) be compact.  Suppose that, on a fixed one-sided
  11: neighbourhood of \(\mathcal Q_0\), the integer-valued Palm gap masses
  12: \(g_q(k)>0\) satisfy the following bounds for some \(r<1\):
  13: \[
  14:  \sup_q g_q(k)\le C(1+k)^m r^k,
  15:  \qquad
  16:  \sup_q|\partial_q^a\log g_q(k)|\le C_a(1+k)^{m_a},
  17:  \quad 1\le |a|\le3.
  18: \tag{SL1}
  19: \]
  20: Assume the same type of polynomial bound for the first two derivatives of
  21: \(\log S_q(k)\), where \(S_q(k)=\sum_{j\ge k}g_q(j)\), and put
  22: \(\mu_q=\sum_{k\ge0}S_q(k)\).  If
  23: \[
  24:  I(q)=\mu_q^{-1}\sum_{k\ge0}g_q(k)
  25:  \dot\ell_q(k)\dot\ell_q(k)^\top,
  26:  \qquad \dot\ell_q=\nabla_q\log g_q,
  27: \tag{SL2}
  28: \]
  29: is positive definite on \(\mathcal Q_0\), then the stationary binary renewal
  30: record is LAN, uniformly over \(q\in\mathcal Q_0\) and bounded admissible
  31: local vectors \(h\):
  32: \[
  33:  \log\frac{dP_{q+h/\sqrt N}^{(N)}}{dP_q^{(N)}}
  34:  =h^\top\Delta_{N,q}-\frac12h^\top I(q)h+o_{P_q}(1),
  35:  \qquad
  36:  \Delta_{N,q}\Rightarrow\mathcal N\{0,I(q)\}.
  37: \tag{SL3}
  38: \]
  39: The convergence of the central sequence and the remainder are compact-uniform.
  40: The conclusion remains valid when some coordinates of \(h\) are restricted
  41: to a closed convex cone.
  42: \end{lemma}
  43: 
  44: \begin{proof}
  45: Let the clicks in \([0,N-1]\) be
  46: \(0\le C_1<\cdots<C_J<N\), set
  47: \[
  48:  A=C_1,\qquad R=N-1-C_J,
  49:  \qquad G_j=C_{j+1}-C_j-1\quad(1\le j<J).
  50: \]
  51: For \(J\ge1\), stationary Palm inversion gives the exact record probability
  52: \[
  53:  P_q^{(N)}(A_0,\ldots,A_{N-1})
  54:  =\frac1{\mu_q}S_q(A)
  55:    \prod_{j=1}^{J-1}g_q(G_j)S_q(R).
  56: \tag{SL4}
  57: \]
  58: Here \(A\) is the forward recurrence (residual life) from the left boundary
  59: and \(R\) is the backward recurrence (age) at the right boundary.  Thus
  60: \(S_q(A)/\mu_q\) is the equilibrium forward-recurrence mass of the first
  61: click, the displayed gaps are complete Palm cycles, and after the last click
  62: the absence of another click contributes \(S_q(R)\).  Formula
  63: \textup{(SL4)} is exact only on \(J\ge1\).  The all-zero record has a separate
  64: probability, bounded by \(CN^{m+1}r^N\), uniformly in \(q\), by summing over
  65: the equilibrium cycle containing the whole window.
  66: 
  67: \Cref{lem:uniform-stopped-renewal-score-main}, applied with
  68: \(K_N=J-1\), gives uniformly in \(q\),
  69: \[
  70:  J/N\longrightarrow1/\mu_q,\qquad
  71:  J=N/\mu_q+O_{P_q}(\sqrt N),\qquad
  72:  \max\{A,R,G_1,\ldots,G_{J-1}\}=O_{P_q}(\log N).
  73: \tag{SL5}
  74: \]
  75: including for every bounded local triangular array.  Taylor's theorem for
  76: \(\log\mu_q\), the polynomial log-tail derivative bound, and
  77: \textup{(SL5)} imply, for bounded \(h\),
  78: \[
  79:  \log\frac{\mu_q}{\mu_{q+h/\sqrt N}}
  80:  +\log\frac{S_{q+h/\sqrt N}(A)}{S_q(A)}
  81:  +\log\frac{S_{q+h/\sqrt N}(R)}{S_q(R)}=o_{P_q}(1)
  82: \tag{SL6}
  83: \]
  84: uniformly.  Thus the increments of the logarithms of the two endpoint factors
  85: and \(\mu_q^{-1}\), rather than those factors themselves, are negligible in
  86: the root-\(N\) local likelihood ratio.
  87: 
  88: Taylor expansion of the complete-gap part of \textup{(SL4)} yields
  89: \[
  90:  \frac1{\sqrt N}\sum_{j=1}^{J-1}h^\top\dot\ell_q(G_j)
  91:  +\frac1{2N}\sum_{j=1}^{J-1}
  92:  h^\top\ddot\ell_q(G_j)h+o_{P_q}(1).
  93: \tag{SL7}
  94: \]
  95: The third-order remainder is uniform by the last assertion of
  96: \Cref{lem:uniform-stopped-renewal-score-main}: after the \(N^{-3/2}\)
  97: Taylor factor, the stopped sum of the common polynomial envelope is
  98: \(o_P(1)\).
  99: Differentiating \(\sum_kg_q(k)=1\), justified by \textup{(SL1)}, gives
 100: \[
 101:  \EE_q\dot\ell_q(G)=0,\qquad
 102:  \EE_q\ddot\ell_q(G)=-\EE_q\{
 103:  \dot\ell_q(G)\dot\ell_q(G)^\top\}.
 104: \tag{SL8}
 105: \]
 106: The stopped Hessian LLN \textup{(U8)} and \textup{(SL8)} turn the second
 107: term in \textup{(SL7)} into \(-h^\top I(q)h/2+o_P(1)\).  The bounded-
 108: Lipschitz stopped-score CLT \textup{(U7)} gives
 109: \[
 110:  \Delta_{N,q}:=N^{-1/2}\sum_{j=1}^{J-1}\dot\ell_q(G_j)
 111:  \Rightarrow\mathcal N\{0,I(q)\}.
 112: \tag{SL9}
 113: \]
 114: The cited stopped-renewal lemma proves these assertions jointly and uniformly,
 115: including under the local triangular arrays.  Combining
 116: \textup{(SL4)}--\textup{(SL9)} proves \textup{(SL3)}.  Restricting local
 117: coordinates to a cone changes only the parameter set of the limit experiment.
 118: \end{proof}
 119: 
 120: \begin{proof}[Proof of \Cref{thm:stationary-two-state-collision-main}]
 121: Let \(W=X_1+X_2\), where the two independent exponential holding times have
 122: rates \(c+d\) and \(c-d\).  Its Laplace transform and the transform of its
 123: continuous survival function are
 124: \[
 125:  \phi_{c,\delta}(s)
 126:  =\frac{c^2-\delta}{(s+c)^2-\delta},
 127:  \qquad
 128:  H_{c,\delta}(s)=\frac{1-\phi_{c,\delta}(s)}s.
 129: \tag{T21}
 130: \]
 131: Differentiation at \(\delta=0\) gives exactly \textup{(SC5)} and
 132: \[
 133:  \partial_cH_{c,0}(s)=-\frac{2c}{(s+c)^3}.
 134: \tag{T22}
 135: \]
 136: Inverse Laplace transformation and sampling at \(t=k\Delta\tau\) show that
 137: \(\partial_\delta S_{c,0}(k)\) has a nonzero cubic coefficient at
 138: \(e^{-c\Delta\tau k}\), whereas \(\partial_cS_{c,0}(k)\) has degree two.
 139: Taking first differences preserves linear independence.  Since every
 140: \(g_{c,0}(k)>0\), a linear combination of the two scores can vanish in
 141: \(L^2(g_{c,0})\) only if the corresponding linear combination of the mass
 142: derivatives, hence of the tail derivatives, vanishes at every \(k\).  The
 143: distinct polynomial degrees then force both coefficients to be zero.  This
 144: proves pointwise positive definiteness in \textup{(SC3)}.
 145: 
 146: On \([\varepsilon,M]\), partial-fraction inversion gives common absolute
 147: bounds
 148: \[
 149:  |\partial_c^a\partial_\delta^b S_{c,\delta}(k)|
 150:  \le C_{a,b}(1+k)^{m_{a,b}}e^{-\varepsilon\Delta\tau k/2}
 151: \tag{T23}
 152: \]
 153: on a fixed neighbourhood with \(c\pm\sqrt\delta>0\).  The relative log-mass
 154: and log-tail bounds do not follow from \textup{(T23)} alone; they follow from
 155: the conditional complete-data argument in
 156: \Cref{lem:uniform-sampled-bin-tail-score-main}, specialized to \(n=2\).
 157: Continuity of \(I_2(c)\), dominated by that lemma, and compactness now give
 158: \textup{(SC6)}.  Applying
 159: \Cref{lem:compact-uniform-stationary-renewal-lan-main} with
 160: \(q=(c,\delta)\) proves \textup{(SC4)} and the half-plane limit.
 161: 
 162: For completeness, the efficient central sequence for the collision
 163: coordinate is
 164: \[
 165:  \Delta_{\delta\cdot c,N}
 166:  =\Delta_{\delta,N}-I_{\delta c}I_{cc}^{-1}\Delta_{c,N},
 167:  \qquad \Var(\Delta_{\delta\cdot c,N})\longrightarrow J_2(c).
 168: \tag{T24}
 169: \]
 170: Replacing \(c\) by the root-\(N\) null recurrence fit and the information
 171: entries by their empirical versions changes the standardized statistic by
 172: \(o_P(1)\), by \Cref{lem:efficient-score-plugin-main}.  Le Cam's third lemma
 173: gives mean \(v\sqrt{J_2(c)}\) under the local alternative.  The
 174: Neyman--Pearson lemma in the residual one-dimensional Gaussian shift gives
 175: \textup{(SC8)} and its envelope; the one-sided likelihood-ratio statistic is
 176: the square of the positive part of the same standardized score.  This is the
 177: standard Gaussian-cone conclusion
 178: \cite{Chernoff1954LikelihoodRatio,SelfLiang1987NonstandardLRT,
 179: vanDerVaart1998AsymptoticStatistics}.
 180: 
 181: We next give an explicit rate-attaining estimator.  From the complete gaps in
 182: the stationary record define
 183: \[
 184:  \widehat S_k=K_N^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^{K_N}\mathbf1_{\{G_j\ge k\}},
 185:  \qquad 0\le k\le3,
 186: \tag{T25}
 187: \]
 188: with an arbitrary fixed value on \(K_N=0\).  The endpoint deletion and the
 189: stopped i.i.d. CLT give
 190: \(\max_{k\le3}|\widehat S_k-S_k|=O_P(N^{-1/2})\) uniformly.  The order-two
 191: tail recurrence is
 192: \[
 193:  S_{k+2}-A S_{k+1}+B S_k=0,\qquad
 194:  A=z_1+z_2,\quad B=z_1z_2,\quad z_i=e^{-\theta_i\Delta\tau}.
 195: \tag{T26}
 196: \]
 197: Its leading Hankel matrix is nonsingular at the double pole by
 198: \Cref{cor:nstate-serial-all-collision-identifiability-main}; compactness makes
 199: the inverse uniform.  Solving the empirical version of \textup{(T26)} gives
 200: \((\widehat A,\widehat B)-(A,B)=O_P(N^{-1/2})\).
 201: 
 202: In a neighbourhood of \(A=2z,B=z^2\), the functions
 203: \[
 204:  c=-\frac1{2\Delta\tau}\log B,\qquad
 205:  \delta=\frac1{(\Delta\tau)^2}
 206:  \left[\operatorname{arcosh}\left(\frac{A}{2\sqrt B}\right)\right]^2
 207: \tag{T27}
 208: \]
 209: are real analytic after continuing the square of \(\operatorname{arcosh}\)
 210: through one.  Let \(\widetilde\delta_N\) be this analytic continuation and
 211: put \(\widehat\delta_N=(\widetilde\delta_N)^+\).  Then
 212: \[
 213:  \widehat c_N-c_N=O_P(N^{-1/2}),\qquad
 214:  \widehat\delta_N-\delta_N=O_P(N^{-1/2})
 215: \tag{T28}
 216: \]
 217: uniformly on bounded collision alternatives.  Because
 218: \(|\sqrt{x^+}-\sqrt{y}|\le\sqrt{|x-y|}\) for \(y\ge0\), the pair
 219: \(\{\!\{\widehat c_N\pm\sqrt{\widehat\delta_N}\}\!\}\) satisfies
 220: \textup{(SC9)}.
 221: 
 222: Finally apply \Cref{lem:two-point-threshold-rate-main} with \(n=2\).  It gives
 223: both the disjoint-ball reduction and the strictly positive Gaussian testing
 224: lower bound, and therefore proves \textup{(SC10)}.  This completes the
 225: two-state result.
 226: \end{proof}

   4: \begin{lemma}[Sampled isolated-double-pole nondegeneracy]
   5: \label{lem:sampled-double-pole-nondegeneracy-main}
   6: On \(\mathcal C_n(\varepsilon,M,c_0)\), the Palm gap family is analytic in
   7: \((\eta,\delta)\) on a fixed physical one-sided neighbourhood of
   8: \(\delta=0\), obeys the relative bounds in \textup{(SL1)} and \textup{(U1)},
   9: and its one-cycle score coordinates are linearly independent.  Consequently
  10: \textup{(SC16)} holds.
  11: \end{lemma}
  12: 
  13: \begin{proof}
  14: Let \(W=X_1+\cdots+X_n\), where the independent exponential holding times
  15: have rates \(c+\sqrt\delta,c-\sqrt\delta,\theta_3,\ldots,\theta_n\), and put
  16: \[
  17:  B_\eta(s)=\prod_{j=3}^n\frac{\theta_j}{s+\theta_j}.
  18: \]
  19: The empty product is one.  The Laplace transform of the continuous survival
  20: function \(\overline F_{\eta,\delta}(t)=P(W>t)\) is
  21: \[
  22:  H_{\eta,\delta}(s)=\frac1s\left\{1-
  23:  \frac{c^2-\delta}{(s+c)^2-\delta}B_\eta(s)\right\}.
  24: \tag{P1}
  25: \]
  26: At a base point with \(c=\lambda\), direct differentiation gives
  27: \[
  28:  \partial_\delta H_{\eta,0}(s)
  29:  =B_\eta(s)\frac{s+2\lambda}{(s+\lambda)^4},
  30:  \qquad
  31:  \partial_cH_{\eta,0}(s)
  32:  =-\frac{2\lambda B_\eta(s)}{(s+\lambda)^3},
  33: \tag{P2}
  34: \]
  35: and, for \(j\ge3\),
  36: \[
  37:  \partial_{\theta_j}H_{\eta,0}(s)
  38:  =-\frac{\lambda^2}{(s+\lambda)^2}
  39:  \frac{1}{(s+\theta_j)^2}
  40:  \prod_{\substack{\ell=3\\\ell\ne j}}^n
  41:  \frac{\theta_\ell}{s+\theta_\ell}.
  42: \tag{P3}
  43: \]
  44: The displayed expression follows after differentiating
  45: \(\theta_j/(s+\theta_j)\) and cancelling its factor \(s\) against the outer
  46: \(1/s\); all remaining numerator factors are nonzero at the relevant
  47: separated poles.
  48: 
  49: Uniform separation makes \(B_\eta(-\lambda)\ne0\).  Thus
  50: \(\partial_\delta H\) has an exact order-four pole at \(-\lambda\), with
  51: nonzero leading coefficient \(\lambda B_\eta(-\lambda)\), while
  52: \(\partial_cH\) has order three there.  At \(-\theta_j\), the derivative in
  53: \(\theta_j\) has order two, and every other coordinate derivative has at most
  54: order one there.  Inverse Laplace transformation therefore gives the following
  55: distinguishing sampled terms:
  56: \[
  57:  \begin{array}{c|c}
  58:  \text{coordinate}&\text{term not attainable by the remaining coordinates}\ \\
  59:  \hline
  60:  \delta& k^3e^{-\lambda\Delta\tau k}\\
  61:  c& k^2e^{-\lambda\Delta\tau k}\quad\text{after the \(\delta\) coefficient is zero}\\
  62:  \theta_j& k e^{-\theta_j\Delta\tau k}\quad(3\le j\le n).
  63:  \end{array}
  64: \tag{P4}
  65: \]
  66: All leading coefficients in \textup{(P4)} are nonzero.
  67: 
  68: Suppose \(a^\top\dot\ell_{\eta,\delta}=0\) in
  69: \(L^2(g_{\eta,0})\).  Full support gives
  70: \(a^\top\partial g_{\eta,0}(k)=0\) for every \(k\).  Absolute summability
  71: then gives the same identity for the tail derivatives.  Exponential-polynomial
  72: sequences at distinct bases are linearly independent: applying successively
  73: the difference operators \(E-z_j\), or equivalently using their rational
  74: generating functions, separates each base and its highest polynomial degree.
  75: The cubic term at \(e^{-\lambda\Delta\tau}\) first forces
  76: \(a_\delta=0\); the unique linear term at every separated base forces
  77: \(a_{\theta_j}=0\); and the remaining quadratic term at the collision base
  78: forces \(a_c=0\).  The scores are therefore linearly independent.
  79: 
  80: It remains to record the absolute analytic control used for information
  81: continuity.  Formula \textup{(P1)} is rational and analytic in
  82: \((\eta,\delta)\) on a common one-sided neighbourhood whose pole clusters
  83: remain separated by compactness and \(c_0\).  Partial fractions, including
  84: the confluent pole at \(-c\), give for every fixed derivative order
  85: \[
  86:  \sup_{(\eta,\delta)}
  87:  |\partial_{\eta,\delta}^a S_{\eta,\delta}(k)|
  88:  \le C_a(1+k)^{m_a}e^{-\varepsilon\Delta\tau k/2}.
  89: \tag{P5}
  90: \]
  91: First differences give the same absolute bound for \(g\).  The required
  92: relative bounds do not follow from \textup{(P5)}; they are proved independently
  93: in \Cref{lem:uniform-sampled-bin-tail-score-main} by conditioning the complete
  94: holding-time scores on a bin or tail event.  Dominated summation therefore
  95: makes the information continuous.  Pointwise positive definiteness,
  96: continuity, and compactness yield the strictly positive uniform minimum in
  97: \textup{(SC16)}.
  98: \end{proof}

 100: \begin{lemma}[Measurable finite-atlas quotient estimator from sampled tails]
 101: \label{lem:serial-collision-recurrence-estimator-main}
 102: Under the restrictions of \Cref{thm:stationary-serial-double-pole-main}, there
 103: are measurable estimators \((\widehat\eta_N,\widehat\delta_N)\), with the
 104: noncollision entries of \(\widehat\eta_N\) canonically ordered and
 105: \(\widehat\delta_N\ge0\), such that for every bounded set of local parameters
 106: \[
 107:  \widehat\eta_N-\eta_N=O_P(N^{-1/2}),
 108:  \qquad
 109:  \widehat\delta_N-\delta_N=O_P(N^{-1/2})
 110: \tag{P6}
 111: \]
 112: uniformly over the compact stratum.  The induced rate multiset satisfies
 113: \textup{(SC19)}.
 114: \end{lemma}
 115: 
 116: \begin{proof}
 117: Delete the initial and terminal incomplete cycles and write the observed
 118: complete gaps as \(G_1,\ldots,G_{K_N}\).  Define
 119: \[
 120:  \widehat S_k=K_N^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^{K_N}\mathbf1_{\{G_j\ge k\}},
 121:  \qquad 0\le k\le2n-1,
 122: \tag{P7}
 123: \]
 124: with arbitrary fixed values on \(K_N=0\).  Apply
 125: \Cref{lem:uniform-stopped-renewal-score-main} to the finite vector of indicator
 126: rewards.  Its stopped CLT and count bound imply
 127: \[
 128:  \max_{0\le k\le2n-1}|\widehat S_k-S_k|=O_P(N^{-1/2})
 129: \tag{P8}
 130: \]
 131: uniformly over the stratum and bounded local alternatives.
 132: 
 133: Write the monic recurrence polynomial as
 134: \[
 135:  \chi(x)=x^n+a_{n-1}x^{n-1}+\cdots+a_0
 136:  =\prod_{i=1}^n(x-z_i),\qquad z_i=e^{-\theta_i\Delta\tau}.
 137: \tag{P9}
 138: \]
 139: The equations
 140: \[
 141:  S_{k+n}+\sum_{j=0}^{n-1}a_jS_{k+j}=0,\qquad0\le k<n,
 142: \tag{P10}
 143: \]
 144: have coefficient matrix \((S_{i+j})_{0\le i,j<n}\).  It is nonsingular even
 145: at collisions by
 146: \Cref{cor:nstate-serial-all-collision-identifiability-main}.  Its determinant
 147: has a positive minimum in absolute value on the compact stratum; the same is
 148: true on a sufficiently small common neighbourhood.  Define
 149: \[
 150:  \widehat H_N=(\widehat S_{i+j})_{0\le i,j<n},
 151:  \qquad
 152:  \widehat s_N=(\widehat S_{n+i})_{0\le i<n},
 153: \]
 154: fix any deterministic \(a^\ast\in\RR^n\), and give the recurrence
 155: coefficient estimator the total definition
 156: \[
 157:  \widehat a_N=
 158:  \begin{cases}
 159:  -\widehat H_N^{-1}\widehat s_N,
 160:  &\lambda_{\min}(\widehat H_N^\top\widehat H_N)>N^{-1/2},\\
 161:  a^\ast,&\text{otherwise}.
 162:  \end{cases}
 163: \tag{P10a}
 164: \]
 165: This is Borel measurable.  The uniform population singular-value bound,
 166: \textup{(P8)}, and Weyl's inequality show that the fallback event has
 167: probability tending uniformly to zero.  Therefore \textup{(P8)} and the
 168: ordinary inverse perturbation identity give
 169: \[
 170:  \max_j|\widehat a_j-a_j|=O_P(N^{-1/2})
 171: \tag{P11}
 172: \]
 173: uniformly.
 174: 
 175: We now distinguish the cluster from the noncollision roots.  In sampled-root
 176: coordinates, the separation in rates gives the common distance
 177: \(\rho_0=\Delta\tau e^{-M\Delta\tau}c_0>0\).  At each base polynomial choose
 178: one circle enclosing its double root and \(n-2\) disjoint circles enclosing
 179: its simple roots, all with radii below \(\rho_0/4\).  On a coefficient
 180: neighbourhood \(U\), the argument principle keeps the root counts equal to
 181: two and one, respectively.  For a simple-root circle the contour power sum
 182: \[
 183:  z_j(a)=\frac{1}{2\pi i}\int_{\gamma_j}
 184:  z\,\frac{\chi_a'(z)}{\chi_a(z)}\,dz
 185: \tag{P12}
 186: \]
 187: is analytic.  On the double-root circle the corresponding first and second
 188: power sums \(p_1,p_2\) are analytic, and
 189: \[
 190:  A=p_1,\qquad B=(p_1^2-p_2)/2
 191: \tag{P13}
 192: \]
 193: are the elementary symmetric functions of the two-root cluster.  These
 194: formulas remain analytic when the two roots split; no individual label is
 195: assigned inside the cluster.
 196: 
 197: The compact collision stratum in coefficient space is covered by finitely
 198: many such neighbourhoods \(U_1,\ldots,U_L\).  Shrink them to open sets
 199: \(V_\ell\) whose closures lie in \(U_\ell\) and still cover the stratum.
 200: Define the chart index to be the least \(\ell\) with
 201: \(\widehat a\in V_\ell\).  Membership in a finite collection of open sets is
 202: Borel measurable.  We verify compatibility on overlaps.  Every chart's
 203: \(n-2\) simple contours retain argument-principle root count one.  At a
 204: collision polynomial no simple contour can contain the double root, because
 205: its argument-principle count would be two; hence every valid chart's
 206: two-root contour encloses the unique double cluster.  After the coefficient
 207: neighbourhoods are made sufficiently small, root continuity and the uniform
 208: cluster separation imply that all valid cluster contours on an overlap
 209: enclose the same two nearby roots.  Their first and second power sums, and
 210: therefore \(A,B\), agree.  The remaining simple-root multisets also agree,
 211: so their vectors agree after numerical ordering by
 212: \(-\log z/\Delta\tau\).  Thus the least-index selection cannot change the
 213: estimand.  The finite maximum of the chart derivatives is bounded.
 214: 
 215: By \textup{(P11)}, for every deterministic sequence \(C_N\to\infty\),
 216: \[
 217:  \sup_qP_q\{\|\widehat a-a(q)\|>C_N/\sqrt N\}\longrightarrow0.
 218: \tag{P14}
 219: \]
 220: The finite shrunken cover has a positive Lebesgue-number margin in coefficient
 221: space.  Coefficients on bounded local alternatives are \(O(N^{-1/2})\) from
 222: the base stratum and hence lie within half that margin for all sufficiently
 223: large \(N\).  Thus \textup{(P14)} implies that the probability of no valid
 224: chart tends to zero uniformly.  On that exceptional event use a fixed ordered
 225: value.
 226: Otherwise the analytic maps, \textup{(P11)}, and the finite derivative bound
 227: give root-\(N\) errors for every ordered simple root and for \(A,B\).  The
 228: separated rates are \(-\log z_j/\Delta\tau\), while the double-cluster
 229: quotient coordinates are the analytic functions in \textup{(T27)}.  Project
 230: the continued \(\widetilde\delta_N\) onto \([0,\infty)\); projection is
 231: nonexpansive.  This proves \textup{(P6)} and the claimed measurability.
 232: 
 233: Finally form the estimated double pair
 234: \(\widehat c_N\pm\sqrt{\widehat\delta_N}\) and the estimated separated
 235: rates.  The square-root inequality used after \textup{(T28)} gives
 236: \(O_P(N^{-1/4})\) for the colliding pair, while all other components are
 237: root-\(N\).  The separation \(c_0\) fixes the optimal matching with
 238: probability tending to one uniformly, proving \textup{(SC19)}.
 239: \end{proof}

 241: \begin{proof}[Proof of \Cref{thm:stationary-serial-double-pole-main}]
 242: The serial killed-reset construction makes the visible record a stationary
 243: renewal record whose Palm cycle is the sampled absorption bin of
 244: \(W=X_1+\cdots+X_n\).  In particular,
 245: \[
 246:  S_{\eta,\delta}(k)=P_{\eta,\delta}
 247:  \{W>k\Delta\tau\},\qquad
 248:  g_{\eta,\delta}(k)=S_{\eta,\delta}(k)-S_{\eta,\delta}(k+1).
 249: \tag{G1}
 250: \]
 251: \Cref{lem:sampled-double-pole-nondegeneracy-main} verifies every analytic,
 252: tail, and information hypothesis of
 253: \Cref{lem:compact-uniform-stationary-renewal-lan-main}.  Applying that lemma
 254: with \(q=(\eta,\delta)\) proves \textup{(SC15)}--\textup{(SC16)}.  Notice
 255: that the proof uses the stationary factorization \textup{(SL4)} on records
 256: containing at least one renewal: its
 257: random number of complete gaps supplies the factor \(1/\mu\) in
 258: \textup{(SC14)}, and its two survival factors and \(1/\mu\) are
 259: such that the increments of their logarithms are \(o_P(1)\) in the local
 260: log likelihood ratio.  The factors themselves are not asserted to be
 261: \(o_P(1)\).  Thus no deterministic-product
 262: equivalence is being assumed.
 263: 
 264: The \(\eta\)-projection of the collision stratum is compact and lies in the
 265: open null slice of the common score neighbourhood in
 266: \Cref{lem:uniform-sampled-bin-tail-score-main}.  A finite ball subcover and a
 267: smaller-radius refinement therefore give a compact \(\mathcal E_0\) whose
 268: interior contains that projection and whose closure remains in the score
 269: chart, as required in part~\textup{(iii)}.
 270: 
 271: For testing, define the population efficient collision central sequence
 272: \[
 273:  \Delta_{\delta\cdot\eta,N}
 274:  =\Delta_{\delta,N}
 275:  -I_{\delta\eta}I_{\eta\eta}^{-1}\Delta_{\eta,N}.
 276: \tag{G2}
 277: \]
 278: It has null variance \(J_n\), which is strictly positive by the Schur
 279: complement of \textup{(SC16)}.  Under
 280: \((\eta_N,\delta_N)=(\eta_0+u/\sqrt N,v/\sqrt N)\), Le Cam's third lemma gives
 281: mean \(vJ_n\); the nuisance shift cancels in \textup{(G2)}.  A null fit from
 282: \Cref{lem:serial-collision-recurrence-estimator-main}, followed by the
 283: empirical residualization displayed in part~\textup{(iii)}, changes
 284: \(\Delta_{\delta\cdot\eta,N}/\sqrt{J_n}\) by \(o_P(1)\) uniformly.  Indeed,
 285: the fit lies in the interior of \(\mathcal E_0\) with probability tending
 286: uniformly to one, while the stopped LLN gives
 287: \(I_N(\widehat\eta_N)\to I_n(\eta_0)\) uniformly.  Uniform positive
 288: definiteness in \textup{(SC16)} then makes the empirical nuisance block and
 289: its Schur complement positive with probability tending uniformly to one.
 290: Thus the gate \(\mathcal G_N\) is asymptotically inactive.  Rejecting above
 291: \(z_{1-\alpha}\) therefore gives \textup{(SC18)}.  The Gaussian
 292: Neyman--Pearson bound after residualizing the nuisance proves the asserted
 293: power envelope.  Finally, the score is continuous on \(\mathcal E_0\), the
 294: empirical information is a finite sum, and eigenvalues and matrix inversion
 295: are continuous on the positive-definite gate.  Together with the Borel
 296: recurrence fit, these facts make \(\mathcal G_N\), \(Z_N\) on that gate, and
 297: the off-gate value \(\phi_N=0\) Borel measurable.  Hence the displayed test
 298: is defined on every binary record.
 299: 
 300: The plug-in assertion in the preceding paragraph is precisely
 301: \Cref{lem:efficient-score-plugin-main}: efficient orthogonality centres the
 302: parameter derivative of the score, while the stopped LLN controls the
 303: estimated information.  It does not rely on the recurrence fit satisfying a
 304: likelihood score equation.
 305: 
 306: The finite-atlas estimator lemma proves the uniform upper rate
 307: \textup{(SC19)}, including the root-\(N\) rate for the centre, collision
 308: square, and canonically ordered noncollision rates.  For the lower bound, fix
 309: a base point and hold \(\eta=\eta_0\) fixed while comparing \(v=0\) with
 310: \(v=v_0>0\).  \Cref{lem:two-point-threshold-rate-main} gives their eventually
 311: exact \(\sqrt{v_0}N^{-1/4}\) matching distance, once
 312: \(N>(2\sqrt{v_0}/c_0)^4\) for \(n>2\), and the positive lower bound
 313: \[
 314:  \Phi_{\rm N}\!\left\{
 315:  -\frac{v_0\sqrt{I_{\delta\delta}(\eta_0)}}2\right\}
 316: \tag{G3}
 317: \]
 318: for the two-point threshold risk.  Together with \textup{(SC19)}, this proves
 319: uniform attainability and pointwise local minimax optimality in rate, with no
 320: claim of an exact minimax constant over a continuum of alternatives.  This
 321: completes the theorem.
 322: \end{proof}

   1: \section{Discussion}\label{sec:discussion}

   3: Theorems~F and G make the collision experiment, rather than the order-two
   4: quotient, the mathematical centre of the article.  For an isolated repeated
   5: rate in a fixed-order sampled generalized-Erlang renewal, the stationary
   6: binary record has a uniform Gaussian half-space experiment in the squared
   7: separation coordinate.  The sampled fourth-order pole proves uniform
   8: nuisance-adjusted information, the residualized score attains the one-sided
   9: power envelope, and the finite-tail recurrence estimator and contiguity
  10: argument match at \(N^{-1/4}\).  The two-state result is the prerequisite
  11: special case, not the endpoint of the extension.
  12: 
  13: At the field level, \Cref{thm:stationary-renewal-palm-equivalence-main} is
  14: logically prior to that application.  It equates the local stationary-window
  15: experiment with an undershot fixed-size Palm-interarrival experiment in both
  16: deficiency directions, transferring bounded-loss decision theory and
  17: semiparametric efficiency rather than only one Gaussian likelihood expansion.
  18: 
  19: The rank-one marked reset turns the visible output of the constrained D-MAP
  20: into a renewal process.  Here the restart law is the point mass at \(D\), but
  21: a fixed nondegenerate restart law would regenerate as well.  This structure
  22: is the source of both the explicit record law and the low-dimensional quotient
  23: inverse.  Arbitrary leakage into the ready state no longer guarantees renewal;
  24: the proof fails when the normalized post-click law depends on the pre-click
  25: state.  Rank-one leakage with mass on both states remains regenerative.
  26: 
  27: The visible law determines the unordered survival pair, not the hidden labels.
  28: The two-state fibre result makes that distinction concrete.  Away from the
  29: exchange diagonal, weakly equivalent stochastic realizations in the
  30: killed-reset cone form a closed arc with the two triangular rate orderings as
  31: endpoints.  On the diagonal the arc collapses.  In higher state dimension the
  32: \((n-1)^2\) orbit calculation applies to the minimal interior stratum and is
  33: not a statement about the global dimension of every visible fibre.
  34: 
  35: The lettered two-state inferential statements A--E remain downstream of the
  36: population algebra.  Theorem~C estimates the three inclusion coordinates;
  37: Theorem~D checks the complete visible law under its stated null and alternative
  38: classes; Theorem~E transports Theorem~C through the stable quotient chart of
  39: Theorem~B.  Sorted roots and log-rates are ordinary delta-method consequences.
  40: The physical-image test is a separate finite-dimensional diagnostic.  The
  41: abstract semiparametric, moving-dimensional coupling, complete-Palm-gap split,
  42: and projection calculations are supplementary and are not used to replace the

  68: record.  Neither super-resolution minimax bound transfers to this paper.

 111: together with the MAP2 nonidentifiability analysis
 112: \cite{RamirezCoboLillo2012WeakEquivalentMAP,
 113: RamirezCoboLilloWiper2010MAP2Nonidentifiability}. &
 114: Weak equivalence fixes the scalar sequence
 115: \(e_D^\top T_0^kT_1\mathbf1\).  We intersect its similarity class with
 116: \(M\mathbf1=\mathbf1\), \(e_D^\top M=e_D^\top\), the killed marked-reset
 117: constraints, and entrywise Markov nonnegativity. &
 118: \Cref{thm:two-state-complete-fibre-arc-main} is an explicit killed-reset
 119: cone-intersection corollary: the feasible transformations form one closed arc,
 120: its endpoints are the rate-swapped triangular kernels, and it collapses at
 121: equal rates. \\
 122: \addlinespace
 123: M\'esz\'aros--Telek canonical discrete MAP2/RAP2 coordinates and the broader
 124: MAP2 canonical-form literature
 125: \cite{MeszarosTelek2013DiscreteMAP2Canonical,
 126: BodrogHeindlHorvathTelek2008MAP2Canonical}. &
 127: For \(T_0=\left(\begin{smallmatrix}p&0\\ b&s\end{smallmatrix}\right)\), the
 128: survival polynomial is
 129: \(x^2-(\operatorname{tr}T_0)x+\det T_0
 130: =x^2-(p+s)x+ps\).  Theorem~B obtains these coefficients from
 131: \((r_0,r_1,r_2)\) through
 132: \((r_2-r_0^2)/(r_1-r_0^2)=p-b\). &
 133: The direct three-inclusion quotient formula and its stability chart are a
 134: candidate original result pending complete reduction against canonical DMAP2
 135: coordinates.  No established priority claim or labelled-kernel inverse is
 136: made. \\
 137: \addlinespace
 138: He--Zhang generalized-Erlang/Coxian representation and minimal Coxian
 139: algorithms \cite{HeZhang2009GeneralizedErlang,HeZhang2008MinimalCoxian}, with
 140: discrete phase-type canonical antecedents
 141: \cite{Cumani1982CanonicalFailure,BobbioEtAl2003AcyclicDPH}. &
 142: For a pure serial sampled kernel, the finite tail is an exponential-polynomial
 143: sequence \(S_k=\sum_j P_j(k)z_j^k\); its annihilating recurrence has roots
 144: \(z_j\), with multiplicities encoded by the polynomial factors \(P_j\). &
 145: \Cref{cor:nstate-serial-all-collision-identifiability-main} is the
 146: finite-coordinate sampled-tail corollary: sufficiently many consecutive tail
 147: coordinates recover the unordered sampled-rate multiset, including repeated
 148: poles.  It is not a general Coxian representation theorem. \\
 149: \addlinespace
 150: General locally conic and loss-of-identifiability theory
 151: \cite{DacunhaCastelleGassiat1997LocallyConic,
 152: LiuShao2003LossIdentifiability}, together with ordinary LAN and Gaussian-shift
 153: optimality \cite{vanDerVaart1998AsymptoticStatistics}. &
 154: The local identifiable coordinate at one isolated serial-rate collision is
 155: \(\delta=\{(\theta_1-\theta_2)/2\}^2\), with all other rates uniformly
 156: separated and the stationary endpoints retained. &
 157: Theorems~F--G prove the model-specific sampled pole-order nondegeneracy,
 158: compact-uniform stationary-record likelihood reduction, efficient collision
 159: test, and matching upper and lower \(N^{-1/4}\) multiset rate for every fixed
 160: serial order. \\
 161: \addlinespace
 162: Finite-mixture singular rates and local minimax theory
 163: \cite{Chen1995FiniteMixtureRate,HoNguyen2019SingularityStructures,
 164: HeinrichKahn2018FiniteMixtureMinimax}. &
 165: Those works show in adjacent mixture models that root coalescence can slow
 166: parameter recovery, and that the rate depends on the model's singularity
 167: structure; in particular, \(N^{-1/4}\) is not a universal collision law. &
 168: They are antecedents for the singular-rate phenomenon, not sources of the
 169: present renewal theorem.  Here the quadratic coordinate and its information
 170: are derived from the exact stationary sampled-gap likelihood, and the upper
 171: rate is paired only with a fixed-base two-point threshold lower bound, not an
 172: exact minimax-risk constant. \\
 173: \addlinespace
 174: Confluent and near-colliding Prony recovery
 175: \cite{BatenkovYomdin2013ConfluentProny,
 176: AkinshinGoldmanYomdin2021NearCollidingProny}. &
 177: The sampled tail is a confluent exponential-polynomial sequence, so its
 178: annihilating recurrence inherits the established instability of recovering
 179: individual near-colliding roots. &
 180: This article does not claim to discover root-collision instability.  Its
 181: increment is to recover regular quotient coordinates through a measurable
 182: finite analytic atlas inside a stationary statistical experiment and to match
 183: the induced \(N^{-1/4}\) root rate with a statistical two-point lower bound. \\
 184: \addlinespace
 185: Bandlimited recovery of a cluster of at most \(p\) near-colliding point
 186: sources \cite{BatenkovGoldmanYomdin2021SuperResolution}. &
 187: That work observes noisy spectral data in a bandwidth \(\Omega\) with
 188: deterministic error at most \(\epsilon\), and obtains cluster-node minimax
 189: error of order
 190: \(\Omega^{-1}{\rm SRF}^{2p-1}\epsilon\), with a corresponding amplitude
 191: rate. &
 192: It is a sharp clustered-source comparator, but its Fourier observation map,
 193: bounded-error experiment, unknown amplitudes, and cluster-size-dependent loss
 194: are absent here.  Its minimax rates therefore do not imply the renewal
 195: two-point threshold rate, nor conversely. \\
 196: \addlinespace
 197: Statistical one-versus-two-source resolution in microscopy
 198: \cite{KulaitisMunkWerner2021Resolution}. &
 199: The null is one point-spread function and the alternative is two equally
 200: weighted translates with the same total intensity.  Under Poisson and
 201: variance-stabilized Gaussian observations, the minimax detection separation
 202: has a fourth-root illumination scale; the homogeneous Gaussian model has a
 203: different pixel-dependent boundary. &
 204: The shared quadratic cancellation is the relevant analogy.  This paper has
 205: Palm interarrival observations transported from a stationary renewal window,
 206: no convolutional point-spread operator or source amplitudes, and proves only
 207: the stated fixed-base two-point threshold lower rate for its pole pair. \\
 208: \addlinespace
 209: Jorgensen--Johnson LAN, information bounds, and efficient estimation for
 210: periodic nonparalyzable dead-time event-detection records
 211: \cite{JorgensenJohnson2026DED}. &
 212: Their non-i.i.d. binary record is generated by periodic gated dead-time event
 213: detection and has regular root-\(N\) parameters.  The present record instead
 214: resets at observed renewals and is reduced by stationary Palm inversion. &
 215: Their result is the closest dead-time LAN comparator, but it does not treat a
 216: generalized-Erlang double-rate collision.  The distinctions are renewal reset
 217: versus periodic gating, loss versus retention of first-order identifiability,
 218: and \(N^{-1/4}\) unordered collision recovery versus regular root-\(N\)
 219: estimation. \\
 220: \addlinespace
 221: Window-censored stationary-renewal likelihood and asymptotic Fisher
 222: information \cite{ZhaoNagaraja2011WindowCensoredRenewal}. &
 223: Their continuous-time likelihood separates the forward recurrence, complete
 224: gaps, right-censored terminal interval, and no-renewal case, and their
 225: information per unit window converges to interarrival information divided by
 226: the mean gap. &
 227: That information identity is prior art for \textup{(LE11)}.  Theorem~4.1 goes
 228: beyond it by proving two-sided Le Cam equivalence with explicit parameter-free
 229: randomizations on the local class, hence bounded-loss risk, local-minimax, and
 230: semiparametric transport. \\
 231: \addlinespace
 232: Kalman minimal-realization uniqueness and MAP reduction
 233: \cite{Kalman1963LinearSystems,TelekHorvath2007MinimalMAP}. &
 234: Reset-preserving similarities satisfy \(M\mathbf1=\mathbf1\) and
 235: \(e_n^\top M=e_n^\top\); positivity is open at a strictly positive minimal
 236: kernel. &
 237: \Cref{thm:nstate-interior-continuum-nonidentifiability-main} identifies a
 238: local immersed \((n-1)^2\)-dimensional orbit only on the minimal interior
 239: stratum.  No global fibre-dimension statement is inferred. \\
 240: \addlinespace
 241: Bickel--Kwon known-marginal Markov tangent and additive nuisance projection
 242: \cite{BickelKwon2001Semiparametric}. &
 243: The supplementary Markov-gap path uses their double-centred interaction space
 244: and additive projection, then imposes \(q(0,0)=0\) and a
 245: positivity-compatible killed-reset realization. &
 246: Only the added atom constraint, its intersection with the declared path class,
 247: calendar-time scaling, and exchange-local calibration remain model-specific.
 248: The double centring and additive projection are attributed to Bickel--Kwon. \\
 249: \addlinespace
 250: Regenerative CLTs, separated batches, and the multivariate delta method
 251: \cite{Janson2024RenewalCLT,AsmussenGlynn2007,
 252: FlegalJones2010BatchMeansSpectral}. &
 253: Complete retained Palm cycles estimate \((r_0,r_1,r_2)\), after which the
 254: stable quotient map gives \((p+s,ps)\). &
 255: Theorems~C and E discharge the stopped-prefix, plug-in-centering, and quotient
 256: transport details.  The sorted-root and log-rate CLTs are not listed as an
 257: independent innovation. \\
 258: \end{longtable}
 259: \endgroup
 260: 
 261: The general renewal equivalence theorem removes the stationary-window and
 262: random-cycle-count difficulty, but it does not broaden the singular geometry.
 263: Theorem~G remains a fixed-serial-order application with one isolated real
 264: double pole, all other poles simple and uniformly separated, a known sampling
 265: interval, and a special positive realization in which every phase is
 266: traversed.  The paper does not characterize when a general phase-type or
 267: matrix-exponential renewal law has a quadratic identifiable collision
 268: coordinate, what happens under residue cancellation, how positivity
 269: restricts root splitting, or which minimax rates occur for multiple,
 270: defective, or complex pole clusters.  Those questions require
 271: positive-realization and representation geometry in addition to rational
 272: pole algebra.  Thus the stationary-renewal experiment transport is broad,
 273: while the singular application deliberately remains confined to the serial
 274: generalized-Erlang family.  General acyclic phase-type and
 275: matrix-exponential models can add positive-realization constraints, pole
 276: cancellation, non-IFR tails, and parameter-dependent hidden paths; treating
 277: them would be a separate representation-and-singularity project.  Likewise,
 278: Markov-renewal and generic MAP observations require a different likelihood
 279: argument because their observed cycles are not i.i.d. Palm interarrivals.
 280: 
 281: \subsection{Sampled-counter interpretation}
 282: 
 283: Continuous dead-time and exponential-recovery detector models motivate the
 284: two-state parametrization
 285: \cite{YuFessler2000,SarbaziSafariHaas2018LongDeadTime,
 286: KrauseWalenta2025SPADRecovery}.  They do not provide the theorem object here:
 287: continuous within-bin recovery after a click can give a marked transition into
 288: the ready state, whereas the present D-MAP latches every click in the dead
 289: state until the boundary.  The sampled counter is therefore an interpretation
 290: of the constrained kernel, not an independently analysed physical system.
 291: A different within-bin protocol would require an explicit check that its
 292: marked kernel retains rank one before the renewal arguments could be used.

The generalized-Erlang representation and its Coxian minimality theory are due
to He--Zhang \cite{HeZhang2009GeneralizedErlang,HeZhang2008MinimalCoxian}.
The following corollary is their serial phase-type structure specialized to
finitely many sampled Palm-tail coordinates; the confluent calculation records
how repeated rates remain recoverable in that specialization.

\begin{corollary}[Finite-coordinate serial specialization with collisions]
\label{cor:nstate-serial-all-collision-identifiability-main}
Fix \(n\ge2\), a known \(\Delta\tau>0\), and arbitrary positive rates
\(\theta=(\theta_1,\ldots,\theta_n)\), with repetitions allowed. Let
\[
Q(\theta)_{ii}=-\theta_i,\qquad
Q(\theta)_{i,i-1}=\theta_i\quad(2\le i\le n),
\]
with all other entries zero, and put
\[
T_0(\theta)=e^{\Delta\tau Q(\theta)},\qquad
T_1(\theta)=(I-T_0(\theta))\mathbf1e_n^\top.
\]
Then the visible record identifies exactly the unordered rate multiset
\(\{\!\{\theta_1,\ldots,\theta_n\}\!\}\). Equivalently, the fibre of the
labelled serial parameter is its \(\mathfrak S_n\)-permutation orbit.

More explicitly, if the distinct rates are
\(\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_r\) with multiplicities
\(m_1,\ldots,m_r\), and \(z_j=e^{-\lambda_j\Delta\tau}\), then the Palm tail
has the confluent Prony form
\[
S_k=\sum_{j=1}^r\sum_{\ell=0}^{m_j-1}
c_{j\ell}k^\ell z_j^k,\qquad c_{j,m_j-1}\ne0,
\]
and its minimal recurrence polynomial is
\[
\chi_\theta(x)=\prod_{j=1}^r(x-z_j)^{m_j}.
\]
The leading \(n\times n\) Hankel matrix
\((S_{i+j})_{0\le i,j<n}\) is invertible; hence
\(S_0,\ldots,S_{2n-1}\) determine \(\chi_\theta\), including all collision
multiplicities. Pole collision therefore changes conditioning and the local
root chart, but does not change population identifiability.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Starting in phase \(n\), the absorption time is
\(W=X_n+\cdots+X_1\), where the \(X_i\) are independent exponentials with
rates \(\theta_i\). Its Laplace transform is
\[
\EE e^{-sW}=\prod_{i=1}^n\frac{\theta_i}{s+\theta_i}.
\]
Consequently
\[
\int_0^\infty e^{-st}\PP(W>t)\,dt
=\frac{1-\prod_{i=1}^n\theta_i/(s+\theta_i)}{s}
\]
has at
\(-\lambda_j\) a pole of exact order \(m_j\). Partial-fraction inversion and
sampling at \(t=k\Delta\tau\) give the displayed exponential-polynomial form
with nonzero top confluent coefficient. Standard confluent Prony algebra
then gives the exact minimal annihilator \(\chi_\theta\)
\cite{KunisRoemerVonDerOhe2020Prony}.

For completeness of the finite-coordinate assertion, the matrices
\(\mathcal O(Q)\) and \(\mathcal C(Q)\) are nonsingular: successive rows
\(e_n^\top Q^j\) and successive columns \(Q^j\mathbf1\) expose the nonzero
bidiagonal products triangularly. Because the exponential is injective on
the real spectrum of \(Q\), Hermite interpolation supplies a polynomial
\(p\) with \(Q=p(e^{\Delta\tau Q})\); hence the corresponding observation and
reachability spaces for \(T_0=e^{\Delta\tau Q}\) are also full. Therefore
\[
(S_{i+j})_{0\le i,j<n}=\mathcal O(T_0)\mathcal C(T_0)
\]
is invertible, and the first \(2n\) tails solve uniquely for the order-\(n\)
recurrence. The roots and their algebraic multiplicities recover
\(\lambda_j=-\Delta\tau^{-1}\log z_j\) and \(m_j\). Conversely, permuting
the independent summands does not change \(W\), the Palm gap law, or the
stationary renewal law. This proves the exact fibre claim.
\end{proof}

reset-preserving similarity group has Lie algebra
\[
\mathfrak g_n=\{B:B\mathbf1=0,\ \beta B=0\},
\qquad \dim\mathfrak g_n=(n-1)^2,
