\section{Stationary collision experiments for sampled serial phase-type renewals}
\label{sec:stationary-serial-collision-main}

This section changes the inferential object from a deterministic product of
complete Palm gaps to the stationary binary record itself.  We first close
that gap for the present two-state sampled counter and then treat one isolated
double collision in an arbitrary fixed serial order.  Throughout this section
the sampling interval \(\Delta\tau>0\) is known.  The record is the lattice
renewal indicator obtained by binning the serial absorption time under the
reset-and-boundary construction; it is not a generic discretely sampled event
process, and multiple post-click renewals within a bin are excluded by that
construction.

For two finite multisets \(A=\{\!\{a_1,\ldots,a_n\}\!\}\) and
\(B=\{\!\{b_1,\ldots,b_n\}\!\}\), write
\[
 d_{\rm m}(A,B)=\min_{\pi\in\mathfrak S_n}
       \max_{1\le i\le n}|a_i-b_{\pi(i)}|
\tag{SC1}
\]
for optimal-matching distance.  This metric retains multiplicities.

\begin{paperthm}[Stationary two-state exchange experiment and sharp recovery]
\label{thm:stationary-two-state-collision-main}
Fix \(0<\varepsilon<M<\infty\).  In the sampled-counter model of
\Cref{ass:model-inference-contract-main}, use the quotient coordinates
\[
 c=\frac{\Gamma+\kappa_{\mathrm r}}2,
 \qquad d=\frac{\Gamma-\kappa_{\mathrm r}}2,
 \qquad \delta=d^2\ge0.
\tag{SC2}
\]
Let \(P_{c,\delta}^{(N)}\) be the law of the stationary binary record
\((A_0,\ldots,A_{N-1})\), and let \(g_{c,\delta}\), \(S_{c,\delta}\), and
\(\mu_{c,\delta}=\sum_{k\ge0}S_{c,\delta}(k)\) denote its Palm gap mass,
tail, and mean cycle length.  At \(\delta=0\), set
\[
 \dot\ell_c(k)=\partial_c\log g_{c,0}(k),\qquad
 \dot\ell_\delta(k)=\partial_\delta\log g_{c,\delta}(k)|_{\delta=0},
\]
and define the calendar information
\[
 I_2(c)=\frac1{\mu_{c,0}}
 \sum_{k\ge0}g_{c,0}(k)
 \begin{pmatrix}\dot\ell_c(k)\\ \dot\ell_\delta(k)\end{pmatrix}
 \begin{pmatrix}\dot\ell_c(k)&\dot\ell_\delta(k)\end{pmatrix}.
\tag{SC3}
\]
Then the following conclusions hold uniformly for \(c\in[\varepsilon,M]\).

\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)},leftmargin=2.6em]
\item If \(u\in\RR\) and \(v\in[0,\infty)\) range over bounded sets, then
\[
 \log\frac{dP_{c+u/\sqrt N,v/\sqrt N}^{(N)}}
               {dP_{c,0}^{(N)}}
 =\begin{pmatrix}u\\v\end{pmatrix}^{\!\top}\Delta_{N,c}
 -\frac12\begin{pmatrix}u\\v\end{pmatrix}^{\!\top}
 I_2(c)\begin{pmatrix}u\\v\end{pmatrix}+o_{P_{c,0}}(1),
\tag{SC4}
\]
where the remainder is uniform in \((c,u,v)\) and
\(\Delta_{N,c}\Rightarrow\mathcal N_2\{0,I_2(c)\}\) uniformly in bounded
Lipschitz distance.  Thus the stationary-record experiments converge to the
Gaussian shift on the half-plane \(\RR\times[0,\infty)\).

\item The continuous survival transform has a double pole at the collision,
whereas its collision derivative has an exact fourth-order pole:
\[
 \mathcal L\{\overline F_{c,\delta}\}(s)
 =\frac1s\left\{1-
 \frac{c^2-\delta}{(s+c)^2-\delta}\right\},
\quad
 \partial_\delta\mathcal L\{\overline F_{c,\delta}\}(s)|_0
 =\frac{s+2c}{(s+c)^4}.
\tag{SC5}
\]
The centre derivative is \(-2c/(s+c)^3\).  Consequently the sampled
collision derivative contains a nonzero
\(k^3e^{-c\Delta\tau k}\) term, while the centre derivative has degree at
most two at that exponential base.  Hence
\[
 \inf_{c\in[\varepsilon,M]}\lambda_{\min}\{I_2(c)\}>0.
\tag{SC6}
\]

\item Partition \(I_2\) according to \((c,\delta)\) and put
\[
 J_2(c)=I_{\delta\delta}
 -I_{\delta c}I_{cc}^{-1}I_{c\delta}>0.
\tag{SC7}
\]
For testing \(H_0:\delta=0\) against \(H_1:\delta>0\), the residualized
score test is asymptotically level \(\alpha\) uniformly in \(c\).  It
coincides with the likelihood-ratio rule only in the limiting Gaussian
half-plane experiment.  At
\((c_N,\delta_N)=(c+u/\sqrt N,v/\sqrt N)\) its limiting power is
\[
 1-\Phi_{\rm N}\{z_{1-\alpha}-v\sqrt{J_2(c)}\}.
\tag{SC8}
\]
This is the Gaussian half-plane power envelope among tests with uniform local
asymptotic level \(\alpha\).

\item There is an estimator \(\widehat{\mathcal R}_N\) of the unordered rate
pair such that, uniformly for bounded \((u,v)\),
\[
 d_{\rm m}\left(
 \widehat{\mathcal R}_N,
 \{\!\{c+u/\sqrt N+\sqrt{v/\sqrt N},
          c+u/\sqrt N-\sqrt{v/\sqrt N}\}\!\}\right)
 =O_P(N^{-1/4}).
\tag{SC9}
\]
The estimated centre is root-\(N\), and the estimator first obtains a
root-\(N\) estimate of \(\delta\) and projects it onto \([0,\infty)\).
Conversely, for every fixed \(c\in(\varepsilon,M)\), \(v_0>0\), and
\(0<a<\sqrt{v_0}/2\),
\[
 \liminf_{N\to\infty}\ \inf_{\widehat{\mathcal R}_N}
 \max_{v\in\{0,v_0\}}
 P_{c,v/\sqrt N}^{(N)}\!\left\{
 N^{1/4}d_{\rm m}(\widehat{\mathcal R}_N,
 \{\!\{c+\sqrt{v/\sqrt N},c-\sqrt{v/\sqrt N}\}\!\})>a
 \right\}>0.
\tag{SC10}
\]
Thus \(N^{-1/4}\) is uniformly attainable and pointwise locally
minimax-optimal in rate, as witnessed by this fixed-base two-point threshold
lower bound.  No exact minimax-risk constant is asserted.  The sign of \(d\)
is not identifiable.
\end{enumerate}
\end{paperthm}

We now impose exactly the isolated-collision restrictions used in the
higher-order result.  Fix \(n\ge2\), \(0<\varepsilon<M<\infty\), and
\(c_0>0\).  The compact double-rate stratum is
\[
\mathcal C_{n}(\varepsilon,M,c_0)=
\left\{(\lambda,\lambda,\lambda_3,\ldots,\lambda_n):
\begin{array}{l}
\lambda,\lambda_j\in[\varepsilon,M],\\
\lambda_3<\cdots<\lambda_n,\\
|\lambda_j-\lambda|\ge c_0,\\
|\lambda_i-\lambda_j|\ge c_0\quad(3\le i<j\le n)
\end{array}\right\}.
\tag{SC11}
\]
Only one double collision is allowed; all other rates are simple and uniformly
separated.  The inequalities in \textup{(SC11)} canonically order the
noncollision rates (and are vacuous for \(n=2\)); these coordinates are not
labels of physical serial states.  No assertion below covers simultaneous
collisions, unknown order, unknown sampling interval, or nonserial phase-type
representations.

\begin{paperthm}[Stationary double-pole experiment for sampled generalized-Erlang renewals]
\label{thm:stationary-serial-double-pole-main}
Fix \(n\), \(\varepsilon,M,c_0\), and known \(\Delta\tau>0\) as above, and
suppose \(\mathcal C_n(\varepsilon,M,c_0)\ne\varnothing\).  For

\[
 Q(\theta)_{ii}=-\theta_i,\qquad
 Q(\theta)_{i,i-1}=\theta_i\quad(2\le i\le n),
\quad K_\theta=e^{\Delta\tau Q(\theta)},
\quad T_{1,\theta}=(I-K_\theta)\mathbf1e_n^\top.
\tag{SC12}
\]
Let \(P_\theta^{(N)}\) be the stationary length-\(N\) binary record from the
killed-reset kernels \((K_\theta,T_{1,\theta})\).  Near the displayed
stratum use
\[
 c=\frac{\theta_1+\theta_2}{2},\qquad
\delta=\left(\frac{\theta_1-\theta_2}{2}\right)^2\ge0,
\qquad \eta=(c,\theta_3,\ldots,\theta_n)\in\RR^{n-1}.
\tag{SC13}
\]
Here and below the separated entries of \(\eta\) are in the canonical order
of \textup{(SC11)}.  Bounded root-\(N\) perturbations preserve this order for
all sufficiently large \(N\), uniformly on the stratum.
Write \(g_{\eta,\delta}\), \(S_{\eta,\delta}\), and
\(\mu_{\eta,\delta}\) for the Palm gap mass, tail, and mean cycle length,

\begin{paperthm}[Stationary double-pole experiment for sampled generalized-Erlang renewals]
\label{thm:stationary-serial-double-pole-main}
Fix \(n\), \(\varepsilon,M,c_0\), and known \(\Delta\tau>0\) as above, and
suppose \(\mathcal C_n(\varepsilon,M,c_0)\ne\varnothing\).  For
\(\theta=(\theta_1,\ldots,\theta_n)\), let
\[
 Q(\theta)_{ii}=-\theta_i,\qquad
 Q(\theta)_{i,i-1}=\theta_i\quad(2\le i\le n),
\quad K_\theta=e^{\Delta\tau Q(\theta)},
\quad T_{1,\theta}=(I-K_\theta)\mathbf1e_n^\top.
\tag{SC12}
\]
Let \(P_\theta^{(N)}\) be the stationary length-\(N\) binary record from the
killed-reset kernels \((K_\theta,T_{1,\theta})\).  Near the displayed
stratum use
\[
 c=\frac{\theta_1+\theta_2}{2},\qquad
\delta=\left(\frac{\theta_1-\theta_2}{2}\right)^2\ge0,
\qquad \eta=(c,\theta_3,\ldots,\theta_n)\in\RR^{n-1}.
\tag{SC13}
\]
Here and below the separated entries of \(\eta\) are in the canonical order
of \textup{(SC11)}.  Bounded root-\(N\) perturbations preserve this order for
all sufficiently large \(N\), uniformly on the stratum.
Write \(g_{\eta,\delta}\), \(S_{\eta,\delta}\), and
\(\mu_{\eta,\delta}\) for the Palm gap mass, tail, and mean cycle length,
and at \((\eta_0,0)\) put
\[
 \dot\ell_{\eta,\delta}(k)
 =\nabla_{(\eta,\delta)}\log g_{\eta,\delta}(k)|_{(\eta_0,0)},
 \qquad
 I_n(\eta_0)=\frac1{\mu_{\eta_0,0}}
 \sum_{k\ge0}g_{\eta_0,0}(k)
 \dot\ell_{\eta,\delta}(k)\dot\ell_{\eta,\delta}(k)^\top.
\tag{SC14}
\]
Then:

\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)},leftmargin=2.6em]
\item For bounded \(u\in\RR^{n-1}\) and \(v\in[0,\infty)\), uniformly over
\((\eta_0,0)\in\mathcal C_n(\varepsilon,M,c_0)\),
\[
 \log\frac{dP_{\eta_0+u/\sqrt N,v/\sqrt N}^{(N)}}
               {dP_{\eta_0,0}^{(N)}}
 =\begin{pmatrix}u\\v\end{pmatrix}^{\!\top}\Delta_{N,\eta_0}
 -\frac12\begin{pmatrix}u\\v\end{pmatrix}^{\!\top}
 I_n(\eta_0)\begin{pmatrix}u\\v\end{pmatrix}
 +o_{P_{\eta_0,0}}(1),
\tag{SC15}
\]
and \(\Delta_{N,\eta_0}\Rightarrow
\mathcal N_n\{0,I_n(\eta_0)\}\) uniformly in bounded Lipschitz distance.
The local stationary-record experiments therefore converge to the Gaussian
shift on \(\RR^{n-1}\times[0,\infty)\).

\item The information is uniformly nondegenerate:
\[
 \inf_{\eta_0\in\mathcal C_n(\varepsilon,M,c_0)}
 \lambda_{\min}\{I_n(\eta_0)\}>0.
\tag{SC16}
\]
This follows from sampled pole order, not merely from population
identifiability: the \(\delta\)-derivative has a nonzero
\(k^3e^{-\lambda\Delta\tau k}\) component; the centre derivative reaches
degree two at that base; and the derivative of each separated rate has a
unique degree-one component at its own exponential base.

\item Partition \(I_n\) according to \((\eta,\delta)\), and set
\[
 J_n=I_{\delta\delta}
 -I_{\delta\eta}I_{\eta\eta}^{-1}I_{\eta\delta}>0.
\tag{SC17}
\]
Choose before observing the record a compact null-coordinate neighbourhood
\(\mathcal E_0\) whose interior contains the \(\eta\)-projection of the
compact stratum and whose closure lies in the common score chart supplied by
\Cref{lem:uniform-sampled-bin-tail-score-main}.  For \(\eta\in\mathcal E_0\),
write
\[
 s_{\eta,0}(k)
 =\left.\nabla_{(\eta,\delta)}\log g_{\eta,\delta}(k)
   \right|_{\delta=0}
 =\begin{pmatrix}s_{\rm nuis}(k;\eta)\\s_\delta(k;\eta)\end{pmatrix},
 \qquad
 I_N(\eta)=\frac1N\sum_{j=1}^{K_N}
 s_{\eta,0}(G_j)s_{\eta,0}(G_j)^\top,
\]
and partition \(I_N\) in the same order; set \(I_N(\eta)=0\) outside
\(\mathcal E_0\).  Define its empirical Schur complement totally by
\[
 J_N(\eta)=
 \begin{cases}
 I_{\delta\delta,N}(\eta)
 -I_{\delta\eta,N}(\eta)I_{\eta\eta,N}(\eta)^{-1}
  I_{\eta\delta,N}(\eta),
 &\eta\in\mathcal E_0\ \text{and}\
  \lambda_{\min}\{I_{\eta\eta,N}(\eta)\}>0,\\
 0,&\text{otherwise}.
 \end{cases}
\]
For the measurable recurrence fit \(\widehat\eta_N\) in
\Cref{lem:serial-collision-recurrence-estimator-main}, let
\[
 \mathcal G_N=\{\widehat\eta_N\in\mathcal E_0,
                 J_N(\widehat\eta_N)>0\}.
\]
On \(\mathcal G_N\), set
\[
 Z_N=\frac{N^{-1/2}\sum_{j=1}^{K_N}
 \left[s_\delta(G_j;\widehat\eta_N)
 -I_{\delta\eta,N}(\widehat\eta_N)
  I_{\eta\eta,N}(\widehat\eta_N)^{-1}
  s_{\rm nuis}(G_j;\widehat\eta_N)\right]}
 {\sqrt{J_N(\widehat\eta_N)}}
\]
and let \(\phi_N=\mathbf1_{\{Z_N>z_{1-\alpha}\}}\); off
\(\mathcal G_N\), define \(\phi_N=0\).  Thus the fit being outside the score
chart, a singular empirical nuisance block, and a nonpositive empirical Schur
complement all give no rejection.  These piecewise definitions and the Borel
recurrence fit make \(\phi_N\) a total measurable function of every binary
record.  This gate is asymptotically inactive uniformly on the stated local
families.  The residualized score test is uniformly asymptotically level
\(\alpha\) and attains the Gaussian half-space
power envelope.  Specifically, \(\phi_N\) has uniform asymptotic level
\(\alpha\) for \(H_0:\delta=0\) and, at \(\delta_N=v/\sqrt N\), has
nuisance-adjusted limiting power
\[
 1-\Phi_{\rm N}\{z_{1-\alpha}-v\sqrt{J_n(\eta_0)}\}.
\tag{SC18}
\]

\item A measurable finite-atlas recurrence estimator based on the first
\(2n\) empirical complete-gap tails gives root-\(N\) estimates of the
canonically ordered \((\eta,\delta)\), after projection of \(\delta\) onto
\([0,\infty)\).  The induced unordered-multiset estimator
\(\widehat{\mathcal R}_{n,N}\) satisfies, uniformly over the compact stratum
and bounded \((u,v)\),
\[
 d_{\rm m}(\widehat{\mathcal R}_{n,N},
 \{\!\{c_N+\sqrt{\delta_N},c_N-\sqrt{\delta_N},
          \theta_{3,N},\ldots,\theta_{n,N}\}\!\})=O_P(N^{-1/4}),
\tag{SC19}
\]
where \((\eta_N,\delta_N)=(\eta_0+u/\sqrt N,v/\sqrt N)\).  The centre and
all canonically ordered separated rates are root-\(N\).

For every fixed point of the stratum, every \(v_0>0\), and every
\(0<a<\sqrt{v_0}/2\), the analogue of \textup{(SC10)}, with the remaining
rates held fixed, has a strictly positive lower limit, bounded below by the
Gaussian two-point testing constant displayed in
\Cref{lem:two-point-threshold-rate-main}.  Hence the unordered-multiset rate
\(N^{-1/4}\) is uniformly attainable over compact bounded local alternatives
and is pointwise locally minimax-optimal in rate at every collision base, as
witnessed by a two-point threshold-risk lower bound.  This is a rate statement,
not an exact asymptotic minimax-risk or sharp-constant theorem.
\end{enumerate}
\end{paperthm}

\noindent\textbf{Limiting-experiment likelihood-ratio remark.}
In the limiting Gaussian half-space experiment, maximizing the quadratic
Gaussian likelihood over \(v\ge0\) gives the same rejection rule as the
residualized score test.  Thus the residualized score test coincides with the
likelihood-ratio test in the limiting Gaussian experiment.  No finite-record
local likelihood-ratio statistic or argmax transfer is asserted.

 succeeded in 222ms:
\subsection{Pole-order nondegeneracy and the fixed-order serial proof}
\label{subsec:serial-pole-order-proof-main}

\begin{lemma}[Sampled isolated-double-pole nondegeneracy]
\label{lem:sampled-double-pole-nondegeneracy-main}
On \(\mathcal C_n(\varepsilon,M,c_0)\), the Palm gap family is analytic in
\((\eta,\delta)\) on a fixed physical one-sided neighbourhood of
\(\delta=0\), obeys the relative bounds in \textup{(SL1)} and \textup{(U1)},
and its one-cycle score coordinates are linearly independent.  Consequently
\textup{(SC16)} holds.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
Let \(W=X_1+\cdots+X_n\), where the independent exponential holding times
have rates \(c+\sqrt\delta,c-\sqrt\delta,\theta_3,\ldots,\theta_n\), and put
\[
 B_\eta(s)=\prod_{j=3}^n\frac{\theta_j}{s+\theta_j}.
\]
The empty product is one.  The Laplace transform of the continuous survival
function \(\overline F_{\eta,\delta}(t)=P(W>t)\) is
\[
 H_{\eta,\delta}(s)=\frac1s\left\{1-
 \frac{c^2-\delta}{(s+c)^2-\delta}B_\eta(s)\right\}.
\tag{P1}
\]
At a base point with \(c=\lambda\), direct differentiation gives
\[
 \partial_\delta H_{\eta,0}(s)
 =B_\eta(s)\frac{s+2\lambda}{(s+\lambda)^4},
 \qquad
 \partial_cH_{\eta,0}(s)
 =-\frac{2\lambda B_\eta(s)}{(s+\lambda)^3},
\tag{P2}
\]
and, for \(j\ge3\),
\[
 \partial_{\theta_j}H_{\eta,0}(s)
 =-\frac{\lambda^2}{(s+\lambda)^2}
 \frac{1}{(s+\theta_j)^2}
 \prod_{\substack{\ell=3\\\ell\ne j}}^n
 \frac{\theta_\ell}{s+\theta_\ell}.
\tag{P3}
\]
The displayed expression follows after differentiating
\(\theta_j/(s+\theta_j)\) and cancelling its factor \(s\) against the outer
\(1/s\); all remaining numerator factors are nonzero at the relevant
separated poles.

Uniform separation makes \(B_\eta(-\lambda)\ne0\).  Thus
\(\partial_\delta H\) has an exact order-four pole at \(-\lambda\), with
nonzero leading coefficient \(\lambda B_\eta(-\lambda)\), while
\(\partial_cH\) has order three there.  At \(-\theta_j\), the derivative in
\(\theta_j\) has order two, and every other coordinate derivative has at most
order one there.  Inverse Laplace transformation therefore gives the following
distinguishing sampled terms:
\[
 \begin{array}{c|c}
 \text{coordinate}&\text{term not attainable by the remaining coordinates}\ \\
 \hline
 \delta& k^3e^{-\lambda\Delta\tau k}\\
 c& k^2e^{-\lambda\Delta\tau k}\quad\text{after the \(\delta\) coefficient is zero}\\
 \theta_j& k e^{-\theta_j\Delta\tau k}\quad(3\le j\le n).
 \end{array}
\tag{P4}
\]
All leading coefficients in \textup{(P4)} are nonzero.

Suppose \(a^\top\dot\ell_{\eta,\delta}=0\) in
\(L^2(g_{\eta,0})\).  Full support gives
\(a^\top\partial g_{\eta,0}(k)=0\) for every \(k\).  Absolute summability
then gives the same identity for the tail derivatives.  Exponential-polynomial
sequences at distinct bases are linearly independent: applying successively
the difference operators \(E-z_j\), or equivalently using their rational
generating functions, separates each base and its highest polynomial degree.
The cubic term at \(e^{-\lambda\Delta\tau}\) first forces
\(a_\delta=0\); the unique linear term at every separated base forces
\(a_{\theta_j}=0\); and the remaining quadratic term at the collision base
forces \(a_c=0\).  The scores are therefore linearly independent.

It remains to record the absolute analytic control used for information
continuity.  Formula \textup{(P1)} is rational and analytic in
\((\eta,\delta)\) on a common one-sided neighbourhood whose pole clusters
remain separated by compactness and \(c_0\).  Partial fractions, including
the confluent pole at \(-c\), give for every fixed derivative order
\[
 \sup_{(\eta,\delta)}
 |\partial_{\eta,\delta}^a S_{\eta,\delta}(k)|
 \le C_a(1+k)^{m_a}e^{-\varepsilon\Delta\tau k/2}.
\tag{P5}
\]
First differences give the same absolute bound for \(g\).  The required
relative bounds do not follow from \textup{(P5)}; they are proved independently
in \Cref{lem:uniform-sampled-bin-tail-score-main} by conditioning the complete
holding-time scores on a bin or tail event.  Dominated summation therefore
makes the information continuous.  Pointwise positive definiteness,
continuity, and compactness yield the strictly positive uniform minimum in
\textup{(SC16)}.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Measurable finite-atlas quotient estimator from sampled tails]
\label{lem:serial-collision-recurrence-estimator-main}
Under the restrictions of \Cref{thm:stationary-serial-double-pole-main}, there
are measurable estimators \((\widehat\eta_N,\widehat\delta_N)\), with the
noncollision entries of \(\widehat\eta_N\) canonically ordered and
\(\widehat\delta_N\ge0\), such that for every bounded set of local parameters
\[
 \widehat\eta_N-\eta_N=O_P(N^{-1/2}),
 \qquad
 \widehat\delta_N-\delta_N=O_P(N^{-1/2})
\tag{P6}
\]
uniformly over the compact stratum.  The induced rate multiset satisfies
\textup{(SC19)}.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
Delete the initial and terminal incomplete cycles and write the observed
complete gaps as \(G_1,\ldots,G_{K_N}\).  Define
\[
 \widehat S_k=K_N^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^{K_N}\mathbf1_{\{G_j\ge k\}},
 \qquad 0\le k\le2n-1,
\tag{P7}
\]
with arbitrary fixed values on \(K_N=0\).  Apply
\Cref{lem:uniform-stopped-renewal-score-main} to the finite vector of indicator
rewards.  Its stopped CLT and count bound imply
\[
 \max_{0\le k\le2n-1}|\widehat S_k-S_k|=O_P(N^{-1/2})
\tag{P8}
\]
uniformly over the stratum and bounded local alternatives.

Write the monic recurrence polynomial as
\[
 \chi(x)=x^n+a_{n-1}x^{n-1}+\cdots+a_0
 =\prod_{i=1}^n(x-z_i),\qquad z_i=e^{-\theta_i\Delta\tau}.
\tag{P9}
\]
The equations
\[
 S_{k+n}+\sum_{j=0}^{n-1}a_jS_{k+j}=0,\qquad0\le k<n,
\tag{P10}
\]
have coefficient matrix \((S_{i+j})_{0\le i,j<n}\).  It is nonsingular even
at collisions by
\Cref{cor:nstate-serial-all-collision-identifiability-main}.  Its determinant
has a positive minimum in absolute value on the compact stratum; the same is
true on a sufficiently small common neighbourhood.  Define
\[
 \widehat H_N=(\widehat S_{i+j})_{0\le i,j<n},
 \qquad
 \widehat s_N=(\widehat S_{n+i})_{0\le i<n},
\]
fix any deterministic \(a^\ast\in\RR^n\), and give the recurrence
coefficient estimator the total definition
\[
 \widehat a_N=
 \begin{cases}
 -\widehat H_N^{-1}\widehat s_N,
 &\lambda_{\min}(\widehat H_N^\top\widehat H_N)>N^{-1/2},\\
 a^\ast,&\text{otherwise}.
 \end{cases}
\tag{P10a}
\]
This is Borel measurable.  The uniform population singular-value bound,
\textup{(P8)}, and Weyl's inequality show that the fallback event has
probability tending uniformly to zero.  Therefore \textup{(P8)} and the
ordinary inverse perturbation identity give
\[
 \max_j|\widehat a_j-a_j|=O_P(N^{-1/2})
\tag{P11}
\]
uniformly.

We now distinguish the cluster from the noncollision roots.  In sampled-root
coordinates, the separation in rates gives the common distance
\(\rho_0=\Delta\tau e^{-M\Delta\tau}c_0>0\).  At each base polynomial choose
one circle enclosing its double root and \(n-2\) disjoint circles enclosing
its simple roots, all with radii below \(\rho_0/4\).  On a coefficient
neighbourhood \(U\), the argument principle keeps the root counts equal to
two and one, respectively.  For a simple-root circle the contour power sum
\[
 z_j(a)=\frac{1}{2\pi i}\int_{\gamma_j}
 z\,\frac{\chi_a'(z)}{\chi_a(z)}\,dz
\tag{P12}
\]
is analytic.  On the double-root circle the corresponding first and second
power sums \(p_1,p_2\) are analytic, and
\[
 A=p_1,\qquad B=(p_1^2-p_2)/2
\tag{P13}
\]
are the elementary symmetric functions of the two-root cluster.  These
formulas remain analytic when the two roots split; no individual label is
assigned inside the cluster.

The compact collision stratum in coefficient space is covered by finitely
many such neighbourhoods \(U_1,\ldots,U_L\).  Shrink them to open sets
\(V_\ell\) whose closures lie in \(U_\ell\) and still cover the stratum.
Define the chart index to be the least \(\ell\) with
\(\widehat a\in V_\ell\).  Membership in a finite collection of open sets is
Borel measurable.  We verify compatibility on overlaps.  Every chart's
\(n-2\) simple contours retain argument-principle root count one.  At a
collision polynomial no simple contour can contain the double root, because
its argument-principle count would be two; hence every valid chart's
two-root contour encloses the unique double cluster.  After the coefficient
neighbourhoods are made sufficiently small, root continuity and the uniform
cluster separation imply that all valid cluster contours on an overlap
enclose the same two nearby roots.  Their first and second power sums, and
therefore \(A,B\), agree.  The remaining simple-root multisets also agree,
so their vectors agree after numerical ordering by
\(-\log z/\Delta\tau\).  Thus the least-index selection cannot change the
estimand.  The finite maximum of the chart derivatives is bounded.

By \textup{(P11)}, for every deterministic sequence \(C_N\to\infty\),
\[
 \sup_qP_q\{\|\widehat a-a(q)\|>C_N/\sqrt N\}\longrightarrow0.
\tag{P14}
\]
The finite shrunken cover has a positive Lebesgue-number margin in coefficient
space.  Coefficients on bounded local alternatives are \(O(N^{-1/2})\) from
the base stratum and hence lie within half that margin for all sufficiently
large \(N\).  Thus \textup{(P14)} implies that the probability of no valid
chart tends to zero uniformly.  On that exceptional event use a fixed ordered
value.
Otherwise the analytic maps, \textup{(P11)}, and the finite derivative bound
give root-\(N\) errors for every ordered simple root and for \(A,B\).  The
separated rates are \(-\log z_j/\Delta\tau\), while the double-cluster
quotient coordinates are the analytic functions in \textup{(T27)}.  Project
the continued \(\widetilde\delta_N\) onto \([0,\infty)\); projection is
nonexpansive.  This proves \textup{(P6)} and the claimed measurability.

Finally form the estimated double pair
\(\widehat c_N\pm\sqrt{\widehat\delta_N}\) and the estimated separated
rates.  The square-root inequality used after \textup{(T28)} gives
\(O_P(N^{-1/4})\) for the colliding pair, while all other components are
root-\(N\).  The separation \(c_0\) fixes the optimal matching with
probability tending to one uniformly, proving \textup{(SC19)}.
\end{proof}

\begin{proof}[Proof of \Cref{thm:stationary-serial-double-pole-main}]
The serial killed-reset construction makes the visible record a stationary
renewal record whose Palm cycle is the sampled absorption bin of
\(W=X_1+\cdots+X_n\).  In particular,
\[
 S_{\eta,\delta}(k)=P_{\eta,\delta}
 \{W>k\Delta\tau\},\qquad
 g_{\eta,\delta}(k)=S_{\eta,\delta}(k)-S_{\eta,\delta}(k+1).
\tag{G1}
\]
\Cref{lem:sampled-double-pole-nondegeneracy-main} verifies every analytic,
tail, and information hypothesis of
\Cref{lem:compact-uniform-stationary-renewal-lan-main}.  Applying that lemma
with \(q=(\eta,\delta)\) proves \textup{(SC15)}--\textup{(SC16)}.  Notice
that the proof uses the stationary factorization \textup{(SL4)} on records
containing at least one renewal: its
random number of complete gaps supplies the factor \(1/\mu\) in
\textup{(SC14)}, and its two survival factors and \(1/\mu\) are
such that the increments of their logarithms are \(o_P(1)\) in the local
log likelihood ratio.  The factors themselves are not asserted to be
\(o_P(1)\).  Thus no deterministic-product
equivalence is being assumed.

The \(\eta\)-projection of the collision stratum is compact and lies in the
open null slice of the common score neighbourhood in
\Cref{lem:uniform-sampled-bin-tail-score-main}.  A finite ball subcover and a
smaller-radius refinement therefore give a compact \(\mathcal E_0\) whose
interior contains that projection and whose closure remains in the score
chart, as required in part~\textup{(iii)}.

For testing, define the population efficient collision central sequence
\[
 \Delta_{\delta\cdot\eta,N}
 =\Delta_{\delta,N}
 -I_{\delta\eta}I_{\eta\eta}^{-1}\Delta_{\eta,N}.
\tag{G2}
\]
It has null variance \(J_n\), which is strictly positive by the Schur
complement of \textup{(SC16)}.  Under
\((\eta_N,\delta_N)=(\eta_0+u/\sqrt N,v/\sqrt N)\), Le Cam's third lemma gives
mean \(vJ_n\); the nuisance shift cancels in \textup{(G2)}.  A null fit from
\Cref{lem:serial-collision-recurrence-estimator-main}, followed by the
empirical residualization displayed in part~\textup{(iii)}, changes
\(\Delta_{\delta\cdot\eta,N}/\sqrt{J_n}\) by \(o_P(1)\) uniformly.  Indeed,
the fit lies in the interior of \(\mathcal E_0\) with probability tending
uniformly to one, while the stopped LLN gives
\(I_N(\widehat\eta_N)\to I_n(\eta_0)\) uniformly.  Uniform positive
definiteness in \textup{(SC16)} then makes the empirical nuisance block and
its Schur complement positive with probability tending uniformly to one.
Thus the gate \(\mathcal G_N\) is asymptotically inactive.  Rejecting above
\(z_{1-\alpha}\) therefore gives \textup{(SC18)}.  The Gaussian
Neyman--Pearson bound after residualizing the nuisance proves the asserted
power envelope.  Finally, the score is continuous on \(\mathcal E_0\), the
empirical information is a finite sum, and eigenvalues and matrix inversion
are continuous on the positive-definite gate.  Together with the Borel
recurrence fit, these facts make \(\mathcal G_N\), \(Z_N\) on that gate, and
the off-gate value \(\phi_N=0\) Borel measurable.  Hence the displayed test
is defined on every binary record.

The plug-in assertion in the preceding paragraph is precisely
\Cref{lem:efficient-score-plugin-main}: efficient orthogonality centres the
parameter derivative of the score, while the stopped LLN controls the
estimated information.  It does not rely on the recurrence fit satisfying a
likelihood score equation.

The finite-atlas estimator lemma proves the uniform upper rate
\textup{(SC19)}, including the root-\(N\) rate for the centre, collision
square, and canonically ordered noncollision rates.  For the lower bound, fix
a base point and hold \(\eta=\eta_0\) fixed while comparing \(v=0\) with
\(v=v_0>0\).  \Cref{lem:two-point-threshold-rate-main} gives their eventually
exact \(\sqrt{v_0}N^{-1/4}\) matching distance, once
\(N>(2\sqrt{v_0}/c_0)^4\) for \(n>2\), and the positive lower bound
\[
 \Phi_{\rm N}\!\left\{
 -\frac{v_0\sqrt{I_{\delta\delta}(\eta_0)}}2\right\}
\tag{G3}
\]
for the two-point threshold risk.  Together with \textup{(SC19)}, this proves
uniform attainability and pointwise local minimax optimality in rate, with no
claim of an exact minimax constant over a continuum of alternatives.  This
completes the theorem.
\end{proof}

\subsection{Stationary likelihood reduction and the two-state proof}
\label{subsec:stationary-renewal-lan-proof-main}

We use the following renewal lemma with a finite-dimensional parameter
\(q\).  Its uniform formulation is included because replacing a deterministic
number of Palm gaps by the stationary record is essential here.

\begin{lemma}[Compact-uniform stationary renewal LAN]
\label{lem:compact-uniform-stationary-renewal-lan-main}
Let \(\mathcal Q_0\) be compact.  Suppose that, on a fixed one-sided
neighbourhood of \(\mathcal Q_0\), the integer-valued Palm gap masses
\(g_q(k)>0\) satisfy the following bounds for some \(r<1\):
\[
 \sup_q g_q(k)\le C(1+k)^m r^k,
 \qquad
 \sup_q|\partial_q^a\log g_q(k)|\le C_a(1+k)^{m_a},
 \quad 1\le |a|\le3.
\tag{SL1}
\]
Assume the same type of polynomial bound for the first two derivatives of
\(\log S_q(k)\), where \(S_q(k)=\sum_{j\ge k}g_q(j)\), and put
\(\mu_q=\sum_{k\ge0}S_q(k)\).  If
\[
 I(q)=\mu_q^{-1}\sum_{k\ge0}g_q(k)
 \dot\ell_q(k)\dot\ell_q(k)^\top,
 \qquad \dot\ell_q=\nabla_q\log g_q,
\tag{SL2}
\]
is positive definite on \(\mathcal Q_0\), then the stationary binary renewal
record is LAN, uniformly over \(q\in\mathcal Q_0\) and bounded admissible
local vectors \(h\):
\[
 \log\frac{dP_{q+h/\sqrt N}^{(N)}}{dP_q^{(N)}}
 =h^\top\Delta_{N,q}-\frac12h^\top I(q)h+o_{P_q}(1),
 \qquad
 \Delta_{N,q}\Rightarrow\mathcal N\{0,I(q)\}.
\tag{SL3}
\]
The convergence of the central sequence and the remainder are compact-uniform.
The conclusion remains valid when some coordinates of \(h\) are restricted
to a closed convex cone.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
Let the clicks in \([0,N-1]\) be
\(0\le C_1<\cdots<C_J<N\), set
\[
 A=C_1,\qquad R=N-1-C_J,
 \qquad G_j=C_{j+1}-C_j-1\quad(1\le j<J).
\]
For \(J\ge1\), stationary Palm inversion gives the exact record probability
\[
 P_q^{(N)}(A_0,\ldots,A_{N-1})
 =\frac1{\mu_q}S_q(A)
   \prod_{j=1}^{J-1}g_q(G_j)S_q(R).
\tag{SL4}
\]
Here \(A\) is the forward recurrence (residual life) from the left boundary
and \(R\) is the backward recurrence (age) at the right boundary.  Thus
\(S_q(A)/\mu_q\) is the equilibrium forward-recurrence mass of the first
click, the displayed gaps are complete Palm cycles, and after the last click
the absence of another click contributes \(S_q(R)\).  Formula
\textup{(SL4)} is exact only on \(J\ge1\).  The all-zero record has a separate
probability, bounded by \(CN^{m+1}r^N\), uniformly in \(q\), by summing over
the equilibrium cycle containing the whole window.

\Cref{lem:uniform-stopped-renewal-score-main}, applied with
\(K_N=J-1\), gives uniformly in \(q\),
\[
 J/N\longrightarrow1/\mu_q,\qquad
 J=N/\mu_q+O_{P_q}(\sqrt N),\qquad
 \max\{A,R,G_1,\ldots,G_{J-1}\}=O_{P_q}(\log N).
\tag{SL5}
\]
including for every bounded local triangular array.  Taylor's theorem for
\(\log\mu_q\), the polynomial log-tail derivative bound, and
\textup{(SL5)} imply, for bounded \(h\),
\[
 \log\frac{\mu_q}{\mu_{q+h/\sqrt N}}
 +\log\frac{S_{q+h/\sqrt N}(A)}{S_q(A)}
 +\log\frac{S_{q+h/\sqrt N}(R)}{S_q(R)}=o_{P_q}(1)
\tag{SL6}
\]
uniformly.  Thus the increments of the logarithms of the two endpoint factors
and \(\mu_q^{-1}\), rather than those factors themselves, are negligible in
the root-\(N\) local likelihood ratio.

Taylor expansion of the complete-gap part of \textup{(SL4)} yields
\[
 \frac1{\sqrt N}\sum_{j=1}^{J-1}h^\top\dot\ell_q(G_j)
 +\frac1{2N}\sum_{j=1}^{J-1}
 h^\top\ddot\ell_q(G_j)h+o_{P_q}(1).
\tag{SL7}
\]
The third-order remainder is uniform by the last assertion of
\Cref{lem:uniform-stopped-renewal-score-main}: after the \(N^{-3/2}\)
Taylor factor, the stopped sum of the common polynomial envelope is
\(o_P(1)\).
Differentiating \(\sum_kg_q(k)=1\), justified by \textup{(SL1)}, gives
\[
 \EE_q\dot\ell_q(G)=0,\qquad
 \EE_q\ddot\ell_q(G)=-\EE_q\{
 \dot\ell_q(G)\dot\ell_q(G)^\top\}.
\tag{SL8}
\]
The stopped Hessian LLN \textup{(U8)} and \textup{(SL8)} turn the second
term in \textup{(SL7)} into \(-h^\top I(q)h/2+o_P(1)\).  The bounded-
Lipschitz stopped-score CLT \textup{(U7)} gives
\[
 \Delta_{N,q}:=N^{-1/2}\sum_{j=1}^{J-1}\dot\ell_q(G_j)
 \Rightarrow\mathcal N\{0,I(q)\}.
\tag{SL9}
\]
The cited stopped-renewal lemma proves these assertions jointly and uniformly,
including under the local triangular arrays.  Combining
\textup{(SL4)}--\textup{(SL9)} proves \textup{(SL3)}.  Restricting local
coordinates to a cone changes only the parameter set of the limit experiment.
\end{proof}

\begin{proof}[Proof of \Cref{thm:stationary-two-state-collision-main}]
Let \(W=X_1+X_2\), where the two independent exponential holding times have
rates \(c+d\) and \(c-d\).  Its Laplace transform and the transform of its
continuous survival function are
\[
 \phi_{c,\delta}(s)
 =\frac{c^2-\delta}{(s+c)^2-\delta},
 \qquad
 H_{c,\delta}(s)=\frac{1-\phi_{c,\delta}(s)}s.
\tag{T21}
\]
Differentiation at \(\delta=0\) gives exactly \textup{(SC5)} and
\[
 \partial_cH_{c,0}(s)=-\frac{2c}{(s+c)^3}.
\tag{T22}
\]
Inverse Laplace transformation and sampling at \(t=k\Delta\tau\) show that
\(\partial_\delta S_{c,0}(k)\) has a nonzero cubic coefficient at
\(e^{-c\Delta\tau k}\), whereas \(\partial_cS_{c,0}(k)\) has degree two.
Taking first differences preserves linear independence.  Since every
\(g_{c,0}(k)>0\), a linear combination of the two scores can vanish in
\(L^2(g_{c,0})\) only if the corresponding linear combination of the mass
derivatives, hence of the tail derivatives, vanishes at every \(k\).  The
distinct polynomial degrees then force both coefficients to be zero.  This
proves pointwise positive definiteness in \textup{(SC3)}.

On \([\varepsilon,M]\), partial-fraction inversion gives common absolute
bounds
\[
 |\partial_c^a\partial_\delta^b S_{c,\delta}(k)|
 \le C_{a,b}(1+k)^{m_{a,b}}e^{-\varepsilon\Delta\tau k/2}
\tag{T23}
\]
on a fixed neighbourhood with \(c\pm\sqrt\delta>0\).  The relative log-mass
and log-tail bounds do not follow from \textup{(T23)} alone; they follow from
the conditional complete-data argument in
\Cref{lem:uniform-sampled-bin-tail-score-main}, specialized to \(n=2\).
Continuity of \(I_2(c)\), dominated by that lemma, and compactness now give
\textup{(SC6)}.  Applying
\Cref{lem:compact-uniform-stationary-renewal-lan-main} with
\(q=(c,\delta)\) proves \textup{(SC4)} and the half-plane limit.

For completeness, the efficient central sequence for the collision
coordinate is
\[
 \Delta_{\delta\cdot c,N}
 =\Delta_{\delta,N}-I_{\delta c}I_{cc}^{-1}\Delta_{c,N},
 \qquad \Var(\Delta_{\delta\cdot c,N})\longrightarrow J_2(c).
\tag{T24}
\]
Replacing \(c\) by the root-\(N\) null recurrence fit and the information
entries by their empirical versions changes the standardized statistic by
\(o_P(1)\), by \Cref{lem:efficient-score-plugin-main}.  Le Cam's third lemma
gives mean \(v\sqrt{J_2(c)}\) under the local alternative.  The
Neyman--Pearson lemma in the residual one-dimensional Gaussian shift gives
\textup{(SC8)} and its envelope; the one-sided likelihood-ratio statistic is
the square of the positive part of the same standardized score.  This is the
standard Gaussian-cone conclusion
\cite{Chernoff1954LikelihoodRatio,SelfLiang1987NonstandardLRT,
vanDerVaart1998AsymptoticStatistics}.

We next give an explicit rate-attaining estimator.  From the complete gaps in
the stationary record define
\[
 \widehat S_k=K_N^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^{K_N}\mathbf1_{\{G_j\ge k\}},
 \qquad 0\le k\le3,
\tag{T25}
\]
with an arbitrary fixed value on \(K_N=0\).  The endpoint deletion and the
stopped i.i.d. CLT give
\(\max_{k\le3}|\widehat S_k-S_k|=O_P(N^{-1/2})\) uniformly.  The order-two
tail recurrence is
\[
 S_{k+2}-A S_{k+1}+B S_k=0,\qquad
 A=z_1+z_2,\quad B=z_1z_2,\quad z_i=e^{-\theta_i\Delta\tau}.
\tag{T26}
\]
Its leading Hankel matrix is nonsingular at the double pole by
\Cref{cor:nstate-serial-all-collision-identifiability-main}; compactness makes
the inverse uniform.  Solving the empirical version of \textup{(T26)} gives
\((\widehat A,\widehat B)-(A,B)=O_P(N^{-1/2})\).

In a neighbourhood of \(A=2z,B=z^2\), the functions
\[
 c=-\frac1{2\Delta\tau}\log B,\qquad
 \delta=\frac1{(\Delta\tau)^2}
 \left[\operatorname{arcosh}\left(\frac{A}{2\sqrt B}\right)\right]^2
\tag{T27}
\]
are real analytic after continuing the square of \(\operatorname{arcosh}\)
through one.  Let \(\widetilde\delta_N\) be this analytic continuation and
put \(\widehat\delta_N=(\widetilde\delta_N)^+\).  Then
\[
 \widehat c_N-c_N=O_P(N^{-1/2}),\qquad
 \widehat\delta_N-\delta_N=O_P(N^{-1/2})
\tag{T28}
\]
uniformly on bounded collision alternatives.  Because
\(|\sqrt{x^+}-\sqrt{y}|\le\sqrt{|x-y|}\) for \(y\ge0\), the pair
\(\{\!\{\widehat c_N\pm\sqrt{\widehat\delta_N}\}\!\}\) satisfies
\textup{(SC9)}.

Finally apply \Cref{lem:two-point-threshold-rate-main} with \(n=2\).  It gives
both the disjoint-ball reduction and the strictly positive Gaussian testing
lower bound, and therefore proves \textup{(SC10)}.  This completes the
two-state result.
\end{proof}

\section{Discussion}\label{sec:discussion}

Theorems~F and G make the collision experiment, rather than the order-two
quotient, the mathematical centre of the article.  For an isolated repeated
rate in a fixed-order sampled generalized-Erlang renewal, the stationary
binary record has a uniform Gaussian half-space experiment in the squared
separation coordinate.  The sampled fourth-order pole proves uniform
nuisance-adjusted information, the residualized score attains the one-sided
power envelope, and the finite-tail recurrence estimator and contiguity
argument match at \(N^{-1/4}\).  The two-state result is the prerequisite
special case, not the endpoint of the extension.

At the field level, \Cref{thm:stationary-renewal-palm-equivalence-main} is
logically prior to that application.  It equates the local stationary-window
experiment with an undershot fixed-size Palm-interarrival experiment in both
deficiency directions, transferring bounded-loss decision theory and
semiparametric efficiency rather than only one Gaussian likelihood expansion.

The rank-one marked reset turns the visible output of the constrained D-MAP
into a renewal process.  Here the restart law is the point mass at \(D\), but
a fixed nondegenerate restart law would regenerate as well.  This structure
is the source of both the explicit record law and the low-dimensional quotient
inverse.  Arbitrary leakage into the ready state no longer guarantees renewal;
the proof fails when the normalized post-click law depends on the pre-click
state.  Rank-one leakage with mass on both states remains regenerative.

The visible law determines the unordered survival pair, not the hidden labels.
The two-state fibre result makes that distinction concrete.  Away from the
exchange diagonal, weakly equivalent stochastic realizations in the
killed-reset cone form a closed arc with the two triangular rate orderings as
endpoints.  On the diagonal the arc collapses.  In higher state dimension the
\((n-1)^2\) orbit calculation applies to the minimal interior stratum and is
not a statement about the global dimension of every visible fibre.

The lettered two-state inferential statements A--E remain downstream of the
population algebra.  Theorem~C estimates the three inclusion coordinates;
Theorem~D checks the complete visible law under its stated null and alternative
classes; Theorem~E transports Theorem~C through the stable quotient chart of
Theorem~B.  Sorted roots and log-rates are ordinary delta-method consequences.
The physical-image test is a separate finite-dimensional diagnostic.  The
abstract semiparametric, moving-dimensional coupling, complete-Palm-gap split,
and projection calculations are supplementary and are not used to replace the
stationary likelihood proof in Theorems~F--G.

\section{Comparison with prior representation and tangent results}
\label{sec:theorem-led-comparison}

\Cref{tab:priority-comparison-main} states the comparison at the formula level.
The middle column identifies the specialization actually used; the last column
states only what remains after that specialization.  In particular, the table
does not treat a change of notation or a standard delta method as a
contribution.

Two statistical resolution comparators are especially close to the visible
\(N^{-1/4}\) rate but do not generate it for this experiment.
Batenkov--Goldman--Yomdin obtain cluster-size-dependent minimax location and
amplitude errors for point sources observed through bandlimited spectral data
with bounded deterministic error
\cite{BatenkovGoldmanYomdin2021SuperResolution}.  Kulaitis--Munk--Werner pose
one blurred source against two equal-intensity sources and derive minimax
detection boundaries under Poisson, variance-stabilized Gaussian, and
homogeneous Gaussian microscopy models
\cite{KulaitisMunkWerner2021Resolution}.  Their Poisson and
variance-stabilized Gaussian separation is proportional to the inverse fourth
root of illumination.  The common fourth-root behavior reflects quadratic
loss of first-order separation information, but the observation operators,
noise laws, parameter classes, and losses differ from the stationary renewal
record.  Neither super-resolution minimax bound transfers to this paper.

To our knowledge, no previous result gives the stationary finite-window LAN
experiment at an isolated rate collision for a sampled generalized-Erlang
renewal record, together with sampled pole-order information nondegeneracy and
matching \(N^{-1/4}\) unordered-rate recovery.  The boundary Gaussian
experiment, singular-rate phenomenon, confluent Prony algebra, and phase-type
representation ingredients each have substantial antecedents cited below;
the contribution is their model-specific stationary-record synthesis and
proof.

Alfa--Neuts D-MAP construction and Zamparo renewal-binary laws and finite-order
Markov criterion \cite{AlfaNeuts1995DMAP,Zamparo2022RenewalBinary}. &
The marked kernel has rank-one form \(T_1=c e_D^\top\), so the weak-law
sequence is
\(g_k=e_D^\top T_0^kT_1\mathbf1\) and finite inclusion probabilities factor
as renewal products. &
Theorem~A evaluates \(g_k\), its equal-rate limit, hazard, covariance mode, and
the exact \(1\)-dependence condition for this triangular killed-reset kernel.
These are model-specific consequences, not a general D-MAP theorem. \\
\addlinespace
Ram\'irez-Cobo--Lillo complete weak-equivalence classification for MAP2/MAP3,
together with the MAP2 nonidentifiability analysis
\cite{RamirezCoboLillo2012WeakEquivalentMAP,
RamirezCoboLilloWiper2010MAP2Nonidentifiability}. &
Weak equivalence fixes the scalar sequence
\(e_D^\top T_0^kT_1\mathbf1\).  We intersect its similarity class with
\(M\mathbf1=\mathbf1\), \(e_D^\top M=e_D^\top\), the killed marked-reset
constraints, and entrywise Markov nonnegativity. &
\Cref{thm:two-state-complete-fibre-arc-main} is an explicit killed-reset
cone-intersection corollary: the feasible transformations form one closed arc,
its endpoints are the rate-swapped triangular kernels, and it collapses at
equal rates. \\
\addlinespace
M\'esz\'aros--Telek canonical discrete MAP2/RAP2 coordinates and the broader
MAP2 canonical-form literature
\cite{MeszarosTelek2013DiscreteMAP2Canonical,
BodrogHeindlHorvathTelek2008MAP2Canonical}. &
For \(T_0=\left(\begin{smallmatrix}p&0\\ b&s\end{smallmatrix}\right)\), the
survival polynomial is
\(x^2-(\operatorname{tr}T_0)x+\det T_0
=x^2-(p+s)x+ps\).  Theorem~B obtains these coefficients from
\((r_0,r_1,r_2)\) through
\((r_2-r_0^2)/(r_1-r_0^2)=p-b\). &
The direct three-inclusion quotient formula and its stability chart are a
candidate original result pending complete reduction against canonical DMAP2
coordinates.  No established priority claim or labelled-kernel inverse is
made. \\
\addlinespace
He--Zhang generalized-Erlang/Coxian representation and minimal Coxian
algorithms \cite{HeZhang2009GeneralizedErlang,HeZhang2008MinimalCoxian}, with
discrete phase-type canonical antecedents
\cite{Cumani1982CanonicalFailure,BobbioEtAl2003AcyclicDPH}. &
For a pure serial sampled kernel, the finite tail is an exponential-polynomial
sequence \(S_k=\sum_j P_j(k)z_j^k\); its annihilating recurrence has roots
\(z_j\), with multiplicities encoded by the polynomial factors \(P_j\). &
\Cref{cor:nstate-serial-all-collision-identifiability-main} is the
finite-coordinate sampled-tail corollary: sufficiently many consecutive tail
coordinates recover the unordered sampled-rate multiset, including repeated
poles.  It is not a general Coxian representation theorem. \\
\addlinespace
General locally conic and loss-of-identifiability theory
\cite{DacunhaCastelleGassiat1997LocallyConic,
LiuShao2003LossIdentifiability}, together with ordinary LAN and Gaussian-shift
optimality \cite{vanDerVaart1998AsymptoticStatistics}. &
The local identifiable coordinate at one isolated serial-rate collision is
\(\delta=\{(\theta_1-\theta_2)/2\}^2\), with all other rates uniformly
separated and the stationary endpoints retained. &
Theorems~F--G prove the model-specific sampled pole-order nondegeneracy,
compact-uniform stationary-record likelihood reduction, efficient collision
test, and matching upper and lower \(N^{-1/4}\) multiset rate for every fixed
serial order. \\
\addlinespace
Finite-mixture singular rates and local minimax theory
\cite{Chen1995FiniteMixtureRate,HoNguyen2019SingularityStructures,
HeinrichKahn2018FiniteMixtureMinimax}. &
Those works show in adjacent mixture models that root coalescence can slow
parameter recovery, and that the rate depends on the model's singularity
structure; in particular, \(N^{-1/4}\) is not a universal collision law. &
They are antecedents for the singular-rate phenomenon, not sources of the
present renewal theorem.  Here the quadratic coordinate and its information
are derived from the exact stationary sampled-gap likelihood, and the upper
rate is paired only with a fixed-base two-point threshold lower bound, not an
exact minimax-risk constant. \\
\addlinespace
Confluent and near-colliding Prony recovery
\cite{BatenkovYomdin2013ConfluentProny,
AkinshinGoldmanYomdin2021NearCollidingProny}. &
The sampled tail is a confluent exponential-polynomial sequence, so its
annihilating recurrence inherits the established instability of recovering
individual near-colliding roots. &
This article does not claim to discover root-collision instability.  Its
increment is to recover regular quotient coordinates through a measurable
finite analytic atlas inside a stationary statistical experiment and to match
the induced \(N^{-1/4}\) root rate with a statistical two-point lower bound. \\
\addlinespace
Bandlimited recovery of a cluster of at most \(p\) near-colliding point
sources \cite{BatenkovGoldmanYomdin2021SuperResolution}. &
That work observes noisy spectral data in a bandwidth \(\Omega\) with
deterministic error at most \(\epsilon\), and obtains cluster-node minimax
error of order
\(\Omega^{-1}{\rm SRF}^{2p-1}\epsilon\), with a corresponding amplitude

+\begin{abstract}
+We prove local asymptotic equivalence, in Le Cam distance, between a
+deterministic window of a stationary lattice renewal indicator and an
+undershot fixed-size independent sample from its Palm interarrival law.  The
+comparison is two-sided and is implemented by explicit parameter-free Markov
+kernels.  It transfers bounded-loss risks, yields Palm information divided by
+mean cycle length as information per unit calendar time, and gives the
+corresponding semiparametric efficiency bound, including after restriction to
+fixed local cones.
+
+We apply this result to one isolated real double pole in a sampled serial
+generalized-Erlang renewal model.  The serial order is fixed, the sampling
+interval is known, all other rates are simple and uniformly separated, and
+the observation uses the serial positive killed-reset realization.  The
+regular collision coordinate is the squared half-separation
+\(\delta=\{(\theta_1-\theta_2)/2\}^2\).  A pole-order argument proves that its
+score is not absorbed by the nuisance scores: the collision, centre, and
+separated-rate derivatives have respectively fourth-, third-, and second-order
+poles.  The stationary experiment is uniformly locally asymptotically normal
+and converges to a Gaussian shift on
+\(\mathbb R^{n-1}\times[0,\infty)\).  The residualized score test attains the
+one-sided local power envelope.  A measurable recurrence estimator attains
+\(N^{-1/4}\) recovery of the unordered colliding rates, and a fixed-base
+two-point threshold lower bound proves optimality in rate.  No exact continuum
+minimax constant and no extension to multiple collisions, unknown order,
+unknown sampling interval, or nonserial phase-type representations is claimed.
+\end{abstract}
+
+\noindent\textbf{Keywords:} asymptotic equivalence; deficiency; stationary
+renewal process; singular LAN; generalized-Erlang distribution; double pole;
+minimax rate
+
+\section{Introduction}
+
+A stationary renewal record observed through a deterministic calendar window
+does not consist of a deterministic number of complete cycles.  The first and
+last cycles are censored, the number of intervening cycles is random, and a
+window may contain no renewal.  These features are harmless for many
+first-order calculations, but they matter when an i.i.d. Palm argument is used
+as a substitute for the actual experiment.  Conditioning a prescribed number
+of cycles to fit in the window is not legitimate: it changes their joint law.
+
+Our first result removes that boundary-cycle problem at the level of
+statistical experiments.  Given a stationary renewal window of length \(N\),
+one kernel extracts the first
+\(m_N=\lfloor N/\mu_0-N^\gamma\rfloor\) complete interarrivals, where
+\(1/2<\gamma<1\).  In the reverse direction, a kernel uses the supplied Palm
+sample and appends base-law cycles after it is exhausted.  The two couplings
+fail only if the record contains too few complete cycles, or if generation in
+the reverse direction needs more than the supplied cycles plus a short
+base-law continuation.  Hellinger locality controls that continuation.  Both
+deficiency directions therefore vanish uniformly, without conditioning Palm
+gaps on fitting inside the window.
+
+The equivalence theorem is useful beyond a parametric model.  Bounded-loss
+procedures transfer in both directions, information per calendar unit is Palm
+information divided by mean cycle length, and an i.i.d. canonical-gradient
+variance is multiplied by mean cycle length.  The same statements remain
+valid for a fixed local cone or constrained local subset, with efficiency and
+minimax bounds interpreted in that restricted experiment.  This qualification
+is essential at a singular boundary.
+
+Our application is the collision of two rates in a sampled serial
+generalized-Erlang renewal law.  If independent exponential holding times have
+rates \(\theta_1,\ldots,\theta_n\), their sum is sampled at a known interval
+\(\Delta\tau\).  At \(\theta_1=\theta_2=\lambda\), the sign of the rate split
+is invisible.  The smooth quotient coordinate is
+\[
+ c=\frac{\theta_1+\theta_2}{2},\qquad
+ \delta=\left(\frac{\theta_1-\theta_2}{2}\right)^2\ge0.
+\]
+Root-\(N\) inference for \(\delta\) therefore becomes fourth-root recovery of
+the unordered pair \(\{\!\{c-\sqrt\delta,c+\sqrt\delta\}\!\}\).
+
+Three ingredients make the singular conclusion statistically complete.
+First, the sampled survival tail is a confluent exponential-polynomial
+sequence whose minimal recurrence and nonsingular leading Hankel matrix give
+regular finite-dimensional quotient coordinates even at collision.  Second,
+the collision derivative has an exact fourth-order pole, whereas the centre
+derivative has order three and each separated-rate derivative has its own
+order-two pole.  After sampling, their distinguishing components are
+\(k^3e^{-\lambda\Delta\tau k}\),
+\(k^2e^{-\lambda\Delta\tau k}\), and
+\(ke^{-\theta_j\Delta\tau k}\).  This proves positive information rather
+than merely population identifiability.  Third, a measurable finite-atlas
+recurrence estimator estimates the regular cluster coordinates at the
+root-\(N\) rate; projection of \(\delta\) onto \([0,\infty)\) and a square
+root yield the attainable \(N^{-1/4}\) multiset rate.  A two-point threshold
+argument supplies the matching lower rate.
+
+The order of the results reflects this logic.  \Cref{thm:stationary-renewal-palm-equivalence-main}
+is the general experiment theorem.  \Cref{prop:serial-tail-coordinates-main}
+isolates the serial recurrence coordinates needed for inference.
+\Cref{prop:sampled-double-pole-nondegeneracy-main} proves score
+nondegeneracy.  \Cref{thm:stationary-serial-double-pole-main} then gives the
+limit experiment, efficient test, and recovery rate.  The two-state model is
+only \Cref{cor:two-state-collision-main}, and the precise lower-rate statement
+is \Cref{lem:two-point-threshold-rate-main}.  Technical derivative bounds,
+the stopped-renewal CLT and LLN, score plug-in equicontinuity, an independent
+direct stationary-likelihood proof, and the finite-atlas construction are in
+the supplement.
+
+Stationary renewal censoring has been studied through its distinct sampling
+patterns and Fisher information \cite{GillKeiding2010RenewalSampling,
+ZhaoNagaraja2011WindowCensoredRenewal}.  Our first theorem strengthens the
+information comparison to two-sided local experiment equivalence and
+decision-theoretic transfer.  General Le Cam theory provides the language for
+deficiency and local minimax risk \cite{LeCamYang2000}, while ordinary LAN and
+Gaussian-shift optimality provide the regular local comparison
+\cite{vanDerVaart1998AsymptoticStatistics}.
+
+The boundary coordinate connects the application to locally conic and
+loss-of-identifiability theory
+\cite{DacunhaCastelleGassiat1997LocallyConic,LiuShao2003LossIdentifiability}
+and to classical boundary likelihood theory
+\cite{Chernoff1954LikelihoodRatio,SelfLiang1987NonstandardLRT}.  The serial
+tail algebra is a finite-coordinate sampled specialization of
+generalized-Erlang and Coxian theory
+\cite{HeZhang2008MinimalCoxian,HeZhang2009GeneralizedErlang}, with confluent
+Prony recovery as an algebraic antecedent
+\cite{BatenkovYomdin2013ConfluentProny,KunisRoemerVonDerOhe2020Prony}.
+Finite-mixture work shows that collision rates depend on the particular
+singularity structure
+\cite{Chen1995FiniteMixtureRate,HeinrichKahn2018FiniteMixtureMinimax,
+HoNguyen2019SingularityStructures}.  The shared fourth-root scale in some
+super-resolution models is not a transferable theorem: their observation
+operators, noise laws, parameter classes, and losses differ from the
+stationary renewal record
+\cite{BatenkovGoldmanYomdin2021SuperResolution,
+KulaitisMunkWerner2021Resolution}.
+
+\subsection*{Observation model and notation}
+
+Let \(W=X_1+\cdots+X_n\), where the \(X_i\) are independent exponentials
+with positive rates \(\theta_i\).  With known \(\Delta\tau>0\), define the
+integer zero-run length \(G\) by
+\[
+ S_\theta(k)=\PP_\theta\{W>k\Delta\tau\},\qquad
+ g_\theta(k)=S_\theta(k)-S_\theta(k+1),\qquad k\ge0,
+\tag{1.1}
+\]
+and the interrenewal length \(D=G+1\), with
+\(\mu_\theta=\EE_\theta D=\sum_{k\ge0}S_\theta(k)\).
+The visible observation is the stationary binary renewal indicator: a one at
+each renewal epoch and zeros otherwise.
+
+Equivalently, in the serial positive realization, let
+\[
+ Q(\theta)_{ii}=-\theta_i,\qquad
+ Q(\theta)_{i,i-1}=\theta_i\quad(2\le i\le n),
+\tag{1.2}
+\]
+with all other entries zero, and put
+\[
+ K_\theta=e^{\Delta\tau Q(\theta)},\qquad
+ T_{1,\theta}=(I-K_\theta)\mathbf1e_n^\top.
+\tag{1.3}
+\]
+The rank-one marked kernel resets after every renewal and gives the Palm law
+in \textup{(1.1)}.  This realization is an assumption of the collision
+theorem.  We do not infer it from a generic discretely sampled event process,
+allow multiple renewals within a bin, or claim the same theorem for a general
+phase-type representation.
+
+For two finite multisets \(A=\{\!\{a_1,\ldots,a_n\}\!\}\) and
+\(B=\{\!\{b_1,\ldots,b_n\}\!\}\), write
+\[
+ d_{\rm m}(A,B)=\min_{\pi\in\mathfrak S_n}
+ \max_{1\le i\le n}|a_i-b_{\pi(i)}|
+\tag{1.4}
+\]
+for matching distance, retaining multiplicities.
+

+\section{Finite serial coordinates at collision}
+
+The next proposition retains only the serial tail facts needed for the
+statistical experiment.  It is not a statement about general phase-type
+representations or similarity fibres.
+
+\begin{proposition}[Confluent sampled-tail coordinates]
+\label{prop:serial-tail-coordinates-main}
+Fix \(n\ge2\), known \(\Delta\tau>0\), and positive rates
+\(\theta=(\theta_1,\ldots,\theta_n)\), with repetitions allowed.  If the
+distinct rates are \(\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_r\), with multiplicities
+\(m_1,\ldots,m_r\), and \(z_j=e^{-\lambda_j\Delta\tau}\), then the sampled
+survival tail in \textup{(1.1)} has the confluent exponential-polynomial form
+\[
+ S_\theta(k)=\sum_{j=1}^r\sum_{\ell=0}^{m_j-1}
+ c_{j\ell}k^\ell z_j^k,qquad c_{j,m_j-1}\ne0.
+\tag{2.1}
+\]
+Its minimal recurrence polynomial is
+\[
+ \chi_\theta(x)=\prod_{j=1}^r(x-z_j)^{m_j}.
+\tag{2.2}
+\]
+The leading \(n\times n\) Hankel matrix
+\((S_\theta(i+j))_{0\le i,j<n}\) is invertible.  Consequently
+\(S_\theta(0),\ldots,S_\theta(2n-1)\) determine \(\chi_\theta\), the
+collision multiplicities, and the unordered sampled-rate multiset
+\(\{\!\{z_1,\ldots,z_1,\ldots,z_r,\ldots,z_r\}\!\}\); known
+\(\Delta\tau\) then recovers the unordered rate multiset.
+\end{proposition}
+
+\begin{proof}
+The Laplace transform of \(W=X_1+\cdots+X_n\) and that of its survival
+function are
+\[
+ \EE e^{-sW}=\prod_{i=1}^n\frac{\theta_i}{s+\theta_i},\qquad
+ \int_0^\infty e^{-st}\PP(W>t)\,dt
+ =\frac{1-\prod_{i=1}^n\theta_i/(s+\theta_i)}s.
+\tag{2.3}
+\]
+The second transform has at \(-\lambda_j\) a pole of exact order \(m_j\).
+Partial-fraction inversion and sampling at \(t=k\Delta\tau\) give
+\textup{(2.1)} with nonzero top confluent coefficient.  Standard confluent
+Prony algebra gives the exact minimal annihilator \textup{(2.2)}
+\cite{KunisRoemerVonDerOhe2020Prony}.
+
+It remains to justify the finite-coordinate claim at repeated roots.  Let
+\(\mathcal O(Q)\) have successive rows \(e_n^\top Q^j\), and let
+\(\mathcal C(Q)\) have successive columns \(Q^j\mathbf1\), for
+\(0\le j<n\).  Both are nonsingular because the nonzero bidiagonal products
+are exposed triangularly.  The exponential is injective on the real spectrum
+of \(Q\), so Hermite interpolation gives a polynomial \(p\) satisfying
+\(Q=p(e^{\Delta\tau Q})\).  The corresponding observation and reachability
+spaces for \(K=e^{\Delta\tau Q}\) are therefore full.  Hence
+\[
+ (S_\theta(i+j))_{0\le i,j<n}=\mathcal O(K)\mathcal C(K)
+\tag{2.4}
+\]
+is invertible.  The first \(2n\) tails uniquely solve the order-\(n\)
+recurrence.  Its roots and algebraic multiplicities recover
+\(\lambda_j=-\Delta\tau^{-1}\log z_j\) and \(m_j\), proving the claim.
+\end{proof}
+

+\begin{abstract}
+We prove local asymptotic equivalence, in Le Cam distance, between a
+deterministic window of a stationary lattice renewal indicator and an
+undershot fixed-size independent sample from its Palm interarrival law.  The
+comparison is two-sided and is implemented by explicit parameter-free Markov
+kernels.  It transfers bounded-loss risks, yields Palm information divided by
+mean cycle length as information per unit calendar time, and gives the
+corresponding semiparametric efficiency bound, including after restriction to
+fixed local cones.
+
+We apply this result to one isolated real double pole in a sampled serial
+generalized-Erlang renewal model.  The serial order is fixed, the sampling
+interval is known, all other rates are simple and uniformly separated, and
+the observation uses the serial positive killed-reset realization.  The
+regular collision coordinate is the squared half-separation
+\(\delta=\{(\theta_1-\theta_2)/2\}^2\).  A pole-order argument proves that its
+score is not absorbed by the nuisance scores: the collision, centre, and
+separated-rate derivatives have respectively fourth-, third-, and second-order
+poles.  The stationary experiment is uniformly locally asymptotically normal
+and converges to a Gaussian shift on
+\(\mathbb R^{n-1}\times[0,\infty)\).  The residualized score test attains the
+one-sided local power envelope.  A measurable recurrence estimator attains
+\(N^{-1/4}\) recovery of the unordered colliding rates, and a fixed-base
+two-point threshold lower bound proves optimality in rate.  No exact continuum
+minimax constant and no extension to multiple collisions, unknown order,
+unknown sampling interval, or nonserial phase-type representations is claimed.
+\end{abstract}
+
+\noindent\textbf{Keywords:} asymptotic equivalence; deficiency; stationary
+renewal process; singular LAN; generalized-Erlang distribution; double pole;
+minimax rate
+
+\section{Introduction}
+
+A stationary renewal record observed through a deterministic calendar window
+does not consist of a deterministic number of complete cycles.  The first and
+last cycles are censored, the number of intervening cycles is random, and a
+window may contain no renewal.  These features are harmless for many
+first-order calculations, but they matter when an i.i.d. Palm argument is used
+as a substitute for the actual experiment.  Conditioning a prescribed number
+of cycles to fit in the window is not legitimate: it changes their joint law.
+
+Our first result removes that boundary-cycle problem at the level of
+statistical experiments.  Given a stationary renewal window of length \(N\),
+one kernel extracts the first
+\(m_N=\lfloor N/\mu_0-N^\gamma\rfloor\) complete interarrivals, where
+\(1/2<\gamma<1\).  In the reverse direction, a kernel uses the supplied Palm
+sample and appends base-law cycles after it is exhausted.  The two couplings
+fail only if the record contains too few complete cycles, or if generation in
+the reverse direction needs more than the supplied cycles plus a short
+base-law continuation.  Hellinger locality controls that continuation.  Both
+deficiency directions therefore vanish uniformly, without conditioning Palm
+gaps on fitting inside the window.
+
+The equivalence theorem is useful beyond a parametric model.  Bounded-loss
+procedures transfer in both directions, information per calendar unit is Palm
+information divided by mean cycle length, and an i.i.d. canonical-gradient
+variance is multiplied by mean cycle length.  The same statements remain
+valid for a fixed local cone or constrained local subset, with efficiency and
+minimax bounds interpreted in that restricted experiment.  This qualification
+is essential at a singular boundary.
+
+Our application is the collision of two rates in a sampled serial
+generalized-Erlang renewal law.  If independent exponential holding times have
+rates \(\theta_1,\ldots,\theta_n\), their sum is sampled at a known interval
+\(\Delta\tau\).  At \(\theta_1=\theta_2=\lambda\), the sign of the rate split
+is invisible.  The smooth quotient coordinate is
+\[
+ c=\frac{\theta_1+\theta_2}{2},\qquad
+ \delta=\left(\frac{\theta_1-\theta_2}{2}\right)^2\ge0.
+\]
+Root-\(N\) inference for \(\delta\) therefore becomes fourth-root recovery of
+the unordered pair \(\{\!\{c-\sqrt\delta,c+\sqrt\delta\}\!\}\).
+
+Three ingredients make the singular conclusion statistically complete.
+First, the sampled survival tail is a confluent exponential-polynomial
+sequence whose minimal recurrence and nonsingular leading Hankel matrix give
+regular finite-dimensional quotient coordinates even at collision.  Second,
+the collision derivative has an exact fourth-order pole, whereas the centre
+derivative has order three and each separated-rate derivative has its own
+order-two pole.  After sampling, their distinguishing components are
+\(k^3e^{-\lambda\Delta\tau k}\),
+\(k^2e^{-\lambda\Delta\tau k}\), and
+\(ke^{-\theta_j\Delta\tau k}\).  This proves positive information rather
+than merely population identifiability.  Third, a measurable finite-atlas
+recurrence estimator estimates the regular cluster coordinates at the
+root-\(N\) rate; projection of \(\delta\) onto \([0,\infty)\) and a square
+root yield the attainable \(N^{-1/4}\) multiset rate.  A two-point threshold
+argument supplies the matching lower rate.
+
+The order of the results reflects this logic.  \Cref{thm:stationary-renewal-palm-equivalence-main}
+is the general experiment theorem.  \Cref{prop:serial-tail-coordinates-main}
+isolates the serial recurrence coordinates needed for inference.
+\Cref{prop:sampled-double-pole-nondegeneracy-main} proves score
+nondegeneracy.  \Cref{thm:stationary-serial-double-pole-main} then gives the
+limit experiment, efficient test, and recovery rate.  The two-state model is
+only \Cref{cor:two-state-collision-main}, and the precise lower-rate statement
+is \Cref{lem:two-point-threshold-rate-main}.  Technical derivative bounds,
+the stopped-renewal CLT and LLN, score plug-in equicontinuity, an independent
+direct stationary-likelihood proof, and the finite-atlas construction are in
+the supplement.
+
+Stationary renewal censoring has been studied through its distinct sampling
+patterns and Fisher information \cite{GillKeiding2010RenewalSampling,
+ZhaoNagaraja2011WindowCensoredRenewal}.  Our first theorem strengthens the
+information comparison to two-sided local experiment equivalence and
+decision-theoretic transfer.  General Le Cam theory provides the language for
+deficiency and local minimax risk \cite{LeCamYang2000}, while ordinary LAN and
+Gaussian-shift optimality provide the regular local comparison
+\cite{vanDerVaart1998AsymptoticStatistics}.
+
+The boundary coordinate connects the application to locally conic and
+loss-of-identifiability theory
+\cite{DacunhaCastelleGassiat1997LocallyConic,LiuShao2003LossIdentifiability}
+and to classical boundary likelihood theory
+\cite{Chernoff1954LikelihoodRatio,SelfLiang1987NonstandardLRT}.  The serial
+tail algebra is a finite-coordinate sampled specialization of
+generalized-Erlang and Coxian theory
+\cite{HeZhang2008MinimalCoxian,HeZhang2009GeneralizedErlang}, with confluent
+Prony recovery as an algebraic antecedent
+\cite{BatenkovYomdin2013ConfluentProny,KunisRoemerVonDerOhe2020Prony}.
+Finite-mixture work shows that collision rates depend on the particular
+singularity structure
+\cite{Chen1995FiniteMixtureRate,HeinrichKahn2018FiniteMixtureMinimax,
+HoNguyen2019SingularityStructures}.  The shared fourth-root scale in some
+super-resolution models is not a transferable theorem: their observation
+operators, noise laws, parameter classes, and losses differ from the
+stationary renewal record
+\cite{BatenkovGoldmanYomdin2021SuperResolution,
+KulaitisMunkWerner2021Resolution}.
+
+\subsection*{Observation model and notation}
+
+Let \(W=X_1+\cdots+X_n\), where the \(X_i\) are independent exponentials
+with positive rates \(\theta_i\).  With known \(\Delta\tau>0\), define the
+integer zero-run length \(G\) by
+\[
+ S_\theta(k)=\PP_\theta\{W>k\Delta\tau\},\qquad
+ g_\theta(k)=S_\theta(k)-S_\theta(k+1),\qquad k\ge0,
+\tag{1.1}
+\]
+and the interrenewal length \(D=G+1\), with
+\(\mu_\theta=\EE_\theta D=\sum_{k\ge0}S_\theta(k)\).
+The visible observation is the stationary binary renewal indicator: a one at
+each renewal epoch and zeros otherwise.
+
+Equivalently, in the serial positive realization, let
+\[
+ Q(\theta)_{ii}=-\theta_i,\qquad
+ Q(\theta)_{i,i-1}=\theta_i\quad(2\le i\le n),
+\tag{1.2}
+\]
+with all other entries zero, and put
+\[
+ K_\theta=e^{\Delta\tau Q(\theta)},\qquad
+ T_{1,\theta}=(I-K_\theta)\mathbf1e_n^\top.
+\tag{1.3}
+\]
+The rank-one marked kernel resets after every renewal and gives the Palm law
+in \textup{(1.1)}.  This realization is an assumption of the collision
+theorem.  We do not infer it from a generic discretely sampled event process,
+allow multiple renewals within a bin, or claim the same theorem for a general
+phase-type representation.
+
+For two finite multisets \(A=\{\!\{a_1,\ldots,a_n\}\!\}\) and
+\(B=\{\!\{b_1,\ldots,b_n\}\!\}\), write
+\[
+ d_{\rm m}(A,B)=\min_{\pi\in\mathfrak S_n}
+ \max_{1\le i\le n}|a_i-b_{\pi(i)}|
+\tag{1.4}
+\]
+for matching distance, retaining multiplicities.
+

+\section{Finite serial coordinates at collision}
+
+The next proposition retains only the serial tail facts needed for the
+statistical experiment.  It is not a statement about general phase-type
+representations or similarity fibres.
+
+\begin{proposition}[Confluent sampled-tail coordinates]
+\label{prop:serial-tail-coordinates-main}
+Fix \(n\ge2\), known \(\Delta\tau>0\), and positive rates
+\(\theta=(\theta_1,\ldots,\theta_n)\), with repetitions allowed.  If the
+distinct rates are \(\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_r\), with multiplicities
+\(m_1,\ldots,m_r\), and \(z_j=e^{-\lambda_j\Delta\tau}\), then the sampled
+survival tail in \textup{(1.1)} has the confluent exponential-polynomial form
+\[
+ S_\theta(k)=\sum_{j=1}^r\sum_{\ell=0}^{m_j-1}
+ c_{j\ell}k^\ell z_j^k,qquad c_{j,m_j-1}\ne0.
+\tag{2.1}
+\]
+Its minimal recurrence polynomial is
+\[
+ \chi_\theta(x)=\prod_{j=1}^r(x-z_j)^{m_j}.
+\tag{2.2}
+\]
+The leading \(n\times n\) Hankel matrix
+\((S_\theta(i+j))_{0\le i,j<n}\) is invertible.  Consequently
+\(S_\theta(0),\ldots,S_\theta(2n-1)\) determine \(\chi_\theta\), the
+collision multiplicities, and the unordered sampled-rate multiset
+\(\{\!\{z_1,\ldots,z_1,\ldots,z_r,\ldots,z_r\}\!\}\); known
+\(\Delta\tau\) then recovers the unordered rate multiset.
+\end{proposition}
+
+\begin{proof}
+The Laplace transform of \(W=X_1+\cdots+X_n\) and that of its survival
+function are
+\[
+ \EE e^{-sW}=\prod_{i=1}^n\frac{\theta_i}{s+\theta_i},\qquad
+ \int_0^\infty e^{-st}\PP(W>t)\,dt
+ =\frac{1-\prod_{i=1}^n\theta_i/(s+\theta_i)}s.
+\tag{2.3}
+\]
+The second transform has at \(-\lambda_j\) a pole of exact order \(m_j\).
+Partial-fraction inversion and sampling at \(t=k\Delta\tau\) give
+\textup{(2.1)} with nonzero top confluent coefficient.  Standard confluent
+Prony algebra gives the exact minimal annihilator \textup{(2.2)}
+\cite{KunisRoemerVonDerOhe2020Prony}.
+
+It remains to justify the finite-coordinate claim at repeated roots.  Let
+\(\mathcal O(Q)\) have successive rows \(e_n^\top Q^j\), and let
+\(\mathcal C(Q)\) have successive columns \(Q^j\mathbf1\), for
+\(0\le j<n\).  Both are nonsingular because the nonzero bidiagonal products
+are exposed triangularly.  The exponential is injective on the real spectrum
+of \(Q\), so Hermite interpolation gives a polynomial \(p\) satisfying
+\(Q=p(e^{\Delta\tau Q})\).  The corresponding observation and reachability
+spaces for \(K=e^{\Delta\tau Q}\) are therefore full.  Hence
+\[
+ (S_\theta(i+j))_{0\le i,j<n}=\mathcal O(K)\mathcal C(K)
+\tag{2.4}
+\]
+is invertible.  The first \(2n\) tails uniquely solve the order-\(n\)
+recurrence.  Its roots and algebraic multiplicities recover
+\(\lambda_j=-\Delta\tau^{-1}\log z_j\) and \(m_j\), proving the claim.
+\end{proof}
+
